acba2abf3522ada0: KUALA LUMPUR: Asian junior champions Ahmad Redzuan Zulwaqqarizal-Low Zi Yu made a commanding start to their World Junior Championships campaign in Cairo on Tuesday.
The top seeds, fresh from helping Malaysia claim silver in the mixed team event on Sunday, needed just 16 minutes to dispatch Canada's Kyle Yatfung Le-Ying Jian 15-5, 15-9 in the second round.
Redzuan-Zi Yu, who received a first-round bye along with the other Malaysian pairs in action, advanced to the last 64 where they will face Brazil's Klecivan Silva-Laura Roviezzo.
The Malaysians carry strong title credentials after capturing the Asian junior crown in Yatsushiro, Japan, in July, ending the country's 19-year wait for the mixed doubles title.
Malaysia enjoyed a perfect day in the mixed doubles with all four combinations advancing to the third round.
Eleventh seeds Khairul Azlan Khashah-Nur Aina Maisarah had to dig deep after dropping the opening game before overcoming India's Yogansh Singh-Aanya Bisht 8-15, 15-6, 15-7.
They next face Australia's Ben Rambaud-Yanxi Liu.
Yusuf Iqbal-Leong Hwee Ling were also convincing in a 15-9, 15-7 victory over Canada's Pitousovanreath Roth-Emma Goyette.
A much tougher assignment awaits them in the last 64 against fourth seeds Filip Titěra-Amélie Maixnerová of the Czech Republic.
Twenty-second seeds Irfan Shazmir-Genevie Lim needed only 13 minutes to dispose of England's Yixiang Hou-Shraddha Gopalakrishnan 15-9, 15-6.
They will next take on Indonesia's Moses Andar Simanjuntak-Reya Azzahra Yulianti.

Malaysia's juniors entered the individual championships with confidence high following their runner-up finish in the Suhandinata Cup, with Redzuan-Zi Yu spearheading hopes of carrying that momentum into the individual event.
f6f951f8e743f136: KULAI: First-time umrah pilgrims from Johor were left disappointed after Malaysia Airlines rescheduled their flight from Senai to Jeddah amid heightened security concerns affecting air travel in Saudi Arabia.
The affected pilgrims, who had spent weeks preparing for their journey, said they accepted the decision while awaiting confirmation of a new departure date.
Umieynoratiqah Abdullah, 27, a financial consultant from Johor Baru, said her travel agency informed her of the rescheduling at 10.40am yesterday.

She was due to travel with her husband and elder sister on Malaysia Airlines flight MH154, scheduled to depart Senai International Airport at 2.50pm for King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah.
"We were initially sad, especially as this was our first umrah trip, but we accept it as Allah's will," she said.
Umieynoratiqah said her travel group comprised about 29 people, including friends and clients, who were also awaiting details of the revised travel arrangements.
She said the agency had yet to provide further information on the replacement flight.
Another pilgrim, customer service officer Muhd Qusyairi Ramli, 26, said he was informed of the rescheduling at 9am yesterday.
He was due to travel with nine family members, including his parents, who had come from Kelantan, for their first umrah pilgrimage.
"We were disappointed because we had been looking forward to the trip for a long time. All our preparations were complete and we were just waiting to depart.
"But we accept the situation and hope we will have the opportunity to go soon," he said.
Qusyairi said the travel agency had informed them that a new departure date would be announced soon, although alternative flight arrangements remained unclear.
Checks at Senai International Airport today found no affected pilgrims at the terminal, as they had been informed of the rescheduling in advance.
Malaysia Airlines rescheduled the direct Senai-Jeddah service amid heightened security concerns affecting air travel in Saudi Arabia.
45cfb4c1592dc9a3: SINGAPORE, Oct 13 — The Titans are coming to Marina Bay Sands, with Attack On Titan: The Musical set to make its South-east Asian debut at Sands Theatre on April 15, 2027.
The stage adaptation of Hajime Isayama’s hit Japanese manga will run until May 2, marking its first Asian engagement outside Japan.
Before Singapore, the show drew audiences in Osaka, Tokyo and New York City between 2023 and 2025.
Presented by Base Entertainment Asia, the production zooms in on the early chapters of the manga, which Isayama first published in 2009.
Those chapters follow humanity as it cowers from giant humanoid creatures known as Titans.
The franchise has since sprawled well beyond the page, spawning an anime series, a live-action film and miniseries, novels, manga spin-offs and video games.
On stage, the story unfolds in Japanese with English subtitles.

It is billed as a 2.5-dimensional musical, a Japanese genre that bridges the flat worlds of manga and anime with the real-life stage by blending live action, musical theatre and cutting-edge technology.
You’ve read the manga, watched the anime, now catch ‘Attack On Titan’ in its Singapore debut in April 2027. — Picture from Instagram/attackontitan_themusical
Steering the production is an all-Japanese creative team made up of director Go Ueki, writer Masafumi Hata, music supervisor Ken The 390 and lyricist Kaori Miura.
Fans can look forward to brand-new songs, along with a nod to the anime’s Season 1 opening theme, Guren No Yumiya.
In a press statement, Base Entertainment Asia chief executive Chantal Prudhomme called the show an “extraordinary leap from manga to the musical stage”.

She said it offers fans another way into a world they know well, gives newcomers to Japanese entertainment a window into an unfamiliar theatrical tradition, and lets musical theatre lovers discover a different style of storytelling.
Tickets are available through Marina Bay Sands Ticketing, Sistic and Klook, and the venue is at 10 Bayfront Avenue.
Early-bird discounts range from 15 per cent to 20 per cent.
Standard tickets are priced from S$58 to S$188 (RM185 to RM600)
Performances run Tuesdays to Fridays at 8pm, Saturdays at 2pm and 8pm, and Sundays at 1.30pm and 6pm.
094d6a8c8a65e4e5: GEORGE TOWN: Schools in Johor, Melaka and Negri Sembilan will be closed tomorrow due to the haze, with selected districts in four other states also affected.

Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the closures would also cover Hulu Langat and Sepang in Selangor; Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin in Pahang; Tawau in Sabah; and Serian, Sri Aman and Lubok Antu in Sarawak.
"Schools in other states and districts will operate as usual," she said in a Facebook post.
During the closure, Fadhlina said Home-Based Teaching and Learning would be implemented, while teachers and members of the support staff would be allowed to work from home.
The announcement comes amid the ongoing haze situation, with the affected schools required to switch to remote learning for the day.
Earlier today, it was reported that 19 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy API readings as of 8am, with Pasir Gudang in Johor recording the highest reading at 180.
Johor was the worst-affected state, with eight areas recording unhealthy readings, according to the Department of Environment's (DoE) Air Pollutant Index Management System.
42c6ff96e01d8184: TEHERAN: Iran will continue its international legal efforts to secure the rights of victims of the Shajareh Tayyebeh school attack in Minab until a final result is achieved, administration spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani says, Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA) reported.
Speaking to IRNA on Tuesday, Mohajerani said the Vice Presidency for Legal Affairs, in cooperation with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, is pursuing the case persistently.

"Even if legal proceedings take 20 years, we will not give up even an iota of the people's rights," she quoted the martyred Leader as saying, adding that the administration remains committed to pursuing the matter with determination and precision until a final outcome is reached.

On the first day of the United States (US)–Israeli war of aggression against Iran on Feb 28, the Shajareh Tayyebeh elementary school in the southern Iranian city of Minab was targeted in a US missile strike, killing at least 175 people, including 168 schoolchildren, sports players, school board members, teachers, and parents.
Mohajerani also pointed to a government decision to establish a special headquarters for Minab to coordinate relief and other initiatives following the attack.
She said the measure was intended to prevent scattered efforts by different organisations and ensure that all activities in the area are carried out in a coordinated manner.
On reconstruction, she said the country's school-building benefactors' association has entered the process and met with the governor of Hormozgan Province.
Under the plan, a new school will be built, while the existing school will be preserved as a museum.
Mohajerani also highlighted cultural efforts to document the tragedy and convey the message of the people's resilience to the world.

The official said Amirkabir Publications has taken the lead in this area, including through the novel "Khoonab-e Minab" (Minab's Blood), written following about 40 days of the author's presence in the area and field interviews with bereaved families.

She expressed hope that translations of the work into different languages would help audiences worldwide understand the suffering and resilience of Minab's people and preserve their story for future generations.
554d21281a4b6aa1: KUALA LUMPUR: Actress Emma Maembong, 34, has been announced as the Malaysian National Winner in the Best Actress in a Leading Role category for her performance in the drama Seadanya Kita at the 2026 Asian Academy Creative Awards (AACA).
The news was shared via an official post on the AACA Instagram account yesterday.
The win qualifies Emma to represent Malaysia at the AACA Grand Gala, which is scheduled to take place on Dec 3.

Alongside Emma, ​​actresses from other countries who won in the same category include Tasma Walton (Australia), Liu Haocun (Mainland China), Charmaine Sheh (Hong Kong SAR), Sobhita Dhulipala (India), Anggun (Indonesia), and Non (Japan).
The AACA finals are scheduled to be held in Singapore this December, where the winners from each category across Asia will vie for the overall championship title.

3f5ec20baa95ca15: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development’s (KPWKM) increased allocation under Budget 2027 will strengthen social protection and the well-being of target groups, including women, children, persons with disabilities (OKU) and the elderly.

Its minister, Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri, said the funding, which rose four per cent to RM4.355 billion, would support various aid initiatives, the development of a care ecosystem and economic empowerment to help target groups realise their potential and become self-reliant.

She said the key initiatives include an increase in Elderly Assistance to RM1.3 billion for nearly 200,000 recipients, and assistance for persons with disabilities to RM1.5 billion for more than 300,000 recipients.
“KPWKM’s priority is to ensure the allocation is translated into services and benefits that are truly felt by the people,” she said at a press conference at Parliament today.

Nancy said the ministry is also focusing on women’s economic empowerment through an approach that combines skills, capital or equipment assistance, support networks and market opportunities to help them generate income.

Among the initiatives are the Madani Well-Being Grant, KIRANA Programme, which provides training, equipment grants and digital marketing guidance, and KASIHNITA, which focuses on personal development and financial management for women, particularly single mothers.

On family well-being, Nancy said the government is continuing the LPPKN BuAi Programme, which offers fertility treatment subsidies of up to RM2,000 per cycle to 2,000 eligible couples, as well as fertility advocacy efforts and men’s wellness services targeting 42,000 individuals.
Meanwhile, Nancy said KPWKM plans to conduct a study to identify the factors behind the rise in stabbing cases in schools and institutions of higher learning.

She said the study is still in the planning stage and requires cooperation from other ministries, while agencies under KPWKM provide counselling services and support to victims, families and individuals who commit such acts.
Among the agencies involved are the Malaysian Board of Counsellors, the Social Welfare Department (JKM), LPPKN and the National Welfare Foundation (YKN).

On efforts to strengthen women’s safety and address femicide, Nancy said KPWKM, through JKM, the Women’s Development Department and YKN, is also working with non-governmental organisations to assist women, including shelter for those unable to return home. — Bernama
dcfd7046d2cd0253: SOFIA: Eleven sailors were missing at sea on Tuesday from a ship sunk by a drone attack off the coast of Bulgaria, the second deadly sinking of a cargo vessel in the area in a week, prompting Bulgaria to summon Russia's ambassador.
Two cargo ships were hit by drones overnight and one was sunk, Bulgarian officials said.
Bulgaria stopped short of explicitly accusing Russia of carrying out the attacks but Prime Minister Rumen Radev said their outcome "benefits the Russian Federation."
There was no immediate comment from Moscow on the incidents.
"This is absolutely unacceptable — another attack in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters," Radev said in a televised address.
The attacks were also condemned by Ukraine and the EU.
"The Black Sea has become another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine," European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on X. "Those responsible should be held accountable."
Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on X on Tuesday that the strike "once again demonstrates Moscow's deliberate disregard for civilian lives."
"The Black Sea is a lifeline for global food security. Russia is attacking it to weaponise hunger and hold the world hostage," he said.
Bulgarian officials said five crew members had been rescued but 11 were still listed as missing from the ship which sank off the coast of the village of Krapets.
Bulgarian media identified the vessel as the cargo ship Azov Concord. Its Turkiye-based manager was not immediately available for comment.
Another ship, the Chelsea 3 sailing under Maltese flag, was also hit by three drones overnight, Bulgarian officials said.
All crew from that ship — seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis — were rescued and none seriously injured.

A week ago nine Syrian sailors and one Egyptian were lost at sea from a ship that sank when hit by drones in Bulgaria's Black Sea exclusive economic zone. Another ship was also hit that night but the crew was rescued.
More than four and a half years into the war that Moscow launched with its full-scale invasion in 2022, Black Sea shipping has increasingly been drawn into a prolonged battle of economic endurance.
Ukraine and Russia are both among the world's largest exporters of grain.
Russia has been bombing Ukraine's Black Sea ports, forcing Ukraine to rely increasingly on river ports on the Danube and shipping routes close to the coasts of Nato members Bulgaria and Romania.
Ukraine, for its part, has increasingly targeted Russian grain-exporting ships in other parts of the Black Sea and the Azov Sea at the mouth of the Don River.

76b845e803f945a1: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department detained 630 foreigners during an enforcement operation at a construction site in Padang Meha, Kulim.

Kedah Immigration director Mohd Ridzzuan Mohd Zain said the 11am operation, dubbed Ops Mega, was conducted yesterday and involved 159 officers from the department's headquarters and offices in Kedah, Perlis, Perak, Kuala Lumpur and Negri Sembilan.
In a social media post today, he said officers inspected 697 people at the construction site.
"Of the 697 people inspected, 630 foreigners aged between 18 and 50 were detained, comprising 622 men and eight women," he said.

Chinese people accounted for the largest group, with 396 detainees, followed by 199 Bangladeshis, 10 Pakistanis, seven people from Myanmar, five Indians, four Ghanaians, three Nigerians, two Kenyans, two Indonesians, one person from New Zealand and one Senegalese.

Ridzzuan said the detainees were arrested for various immigration offences under Sections 6(1)(c) and 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, and Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963.
"Six witness summonses were also issued to assist investigations.
"The operation faced several challenges, including attempts by some detainees to flee by hiding in high-risk areas and climbing onto the roofs of unfinished buildings.
"Provocative actions by a group of detainees against immigration officers also created tension, requiring our personnel to act swiftly to bring the situation under control," he said.
Ridzzuan said heavy rain further complicated the operation, leaving surfaces slippery and access routes muddy.
"Unfinished building structures, elevator shafts, exposed reinforcement bars, scattered construction materials, heavy machinery and work at heights also posed safety risks to our officers," he said.
He reminded employers, main contractors and subcontractors to ensure that all foreign workers had valid travel documents and immigration passes or permits, and complied with immigration requirements.
"The department will continue to intensify enforcement to ensure compliance with the country's immigration laws," he added.
4728972ecab29aa6: KUALA LUMPUR: Independent shuttler Lee Zii Jia has applied to the Kuala Lumpur High Court for an order to allow an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) of LZJ Management Sdn Bhd to proceed following the failure of an earlier meeting.

The application, filed on July 2, was not based on allegations of misconduct between the parties involved, but was intended to obtain a court order to hold the company's EGM, his lawyer, Ahmad Zayd Ahmad Zuber of Messrs Faisal & Zayd, said.

Ahmad Zayd said Zii Jia was also seeking an interim injunction to restrain his father, Lee Chee Hin, and his sister, Lee Zii Yii, from making certain financial and management decisions concerning LZJ Management while the legal dispute remained ongoing.
"What we are essentially seeking is an application to hold an EGM of the company," he said when contacted.
"There are no allegations against any of the parties involved. We are simply seeking the court's assistance to hold the EGM in accordance with the terms requested."
However, Ahmad Zayd declined to disclose in detail the main reasons Zii Jia had sought to convene the EGM.

According to the supporting affidavit, Zii Jia's attempt to hold an EGM on Dec 22 last year failed after Chee Hin, Zii Yii, and his younger brother, Lee Tao, did not attend despite having been given notice.
Their absence meant the meeting could not proceed because the quorum required under the Companies Act 2016 was not met.
Zii Jia was also said to have made efforts to contact his family members privately before exploring several other avenues, including seeking assistance from the Companies Commission of Malaysia.

The supporting affidavit stated that LZJ Management was facing a management and administrative deadlock, and that it was impractical or potentially impossible to convene a meeting through normal procedures under the Companies Act.
Through the application, Zii Jia is seeking authorisation to convene the EGM, issue the meeting notice, and appoint an independent chairman to preside over the proceedings.

He is also seeking an order allowing resolutions passed through voting based on shareholdings to be lawfully implemented, including matters relating to the removal of existing directors, the appointment of new directors, and the appointment of a new company secretary.
Besides Chee Hin, Zii Yii, and Tao, LZJ Management was also named as a respondent.

In his application for an interim injunction, Zii Jia is seeking to restrain Chee Hin and Zii Yii from approving or paying themselves directors' fees, allowances, bonuses, and other financial benefits beyond their respective monthly salaries.

He is also seeking restrictions on decisions relating to the appointment or removal of directors, the appointment of a company secretary, the disposal of material assets, the issuance of new shares, and changes to the shareholding structure without the court's permission.
According to the application, Zii Jia holds a 90 per cent stake in LZJ Management, while Zii Yii holds nine per cent and Tao holds one per cent.
The hearing is scheduled for Nov 25.
2bd6f2190c6c3468: MADRID: Former Real Madrid defender Dani Carvajal signed for Getafe on Tuesday as a free agent until the end of the season.
The 34-year-old right-back left Los Blancos, with whom he won 27 trophies, at the end of last season.
"Getafe have reached a deal with Dani Carvajal that will keep him at the club until June 30, 2027," said the La Liga side in a statement, highlighting his "leadership and experience."
Carvajal came through Real Madrid's La Fabrica youth academy and, after he left for Bayer Leverkusen in 2012, returned to the Spanish giants the following summer.
The defender was hampered by injury for much of last season and was not called up to join Spain's squad as La Roja won the World Cup. - AFP
d129cb0bf4a53fb1: SHAH ALAM: A lorry driver who crashed into 11 cars at a traffic light intersection along Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari in Alam Budiman last Friday will be charged at the Shah Alam magistrate's court tomorrow.
Shah Alam district police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said the suspect would be charged under Section 44(1A)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
"Tomorrow, the accused arrested in connection with the crash involving 12 vehicles at the Alam Budiman traffic light intersection will be charged at the Shah Alam magistrate's court," he said today.
Four people were injured in the crash, including a man who was seriously hurt.
The 51-year-old driver, who tested positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine, was remanded for four days to assist in investigations following the incident.
b0754eb1bb34f8cf: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 13 — Johor police opened 9,897 investigation papers involving commercial crimes in the first nine months of this year, with losses totalling RM212.64 million.

Its chief, Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad, said the figure represented an increase of 3,036 cases from the 6,861 recorded during the same period last year, although financial losses declined from RM252.57 million.
He said more than 90 per cent of the cases reported between Jan 1 and Sept 30 involved online scams.

“The increase in reported cases calls for more proactive measures. Fraud and scams continue to evolve alongside technological advances and an increasingly sophisticated digital landscape,” he said at the Johor Police contingent’s monthly assembly here today.
Ab Rahaman said the state’s crime index also rose to 4,343 cases during the same period, compared with 4,152 last year.
Violent crimes increased to 1,123 cases from 981, while property crimes rose to 3,220 from 3,171, he added.

Separately, Ab Rahaman said police were awaiting instructions and a formal decision from the Johor State Prosecutor’s Office on whether to charge the suspect in the murder of Form Four student Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal.
He said the investigation papers on the case were referred to the office on October 9.
“The suspect is a juvenile, and this requires more careful consideration by the Johor State Prosecution Director,” he said.
Irene Sofiya was found unconscious and covered in blood at a school hall in Yong Peng, Batu Pahat, at about 5pm on October 3. She was later pronounced dead.
A 16-year-old boy was remanded for six days from October 4 to assist investigations, with the remand subsequently extended for another six days until Friday. — Bernama
13768e5dca71424b: KUALA LUMPUR: NWE Resources Group Bhd's initial public offering (IPO) portion made available to the Malaysian public was oversubscribed by 2.82 times ahead of its listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the company said a total of 3,068 applications for 103.16 million issue shares were received from the Malaysian public.
"For the Bumiputera portion, a total of 1,536 applications for 38.93 million issue shares were received, representing an oversubscription rate of 1.88 times.
"For the public portion, a total of 1,532 applications for 64.23 million issue shares were received, representing an oversubscription rate of 3.76 times," it added.
NWE Resources said the 10.8 million issue shares made available for application by eligible persons had been fully subscribed.
Meanwhile, the 105.34 million issue shares made available by way of private placement to selected investors had been fully placed out by the placement agent, it said.
The company said the private placement shares had been allocated to 16 identified investors, with none becoming a substantial shareholder arising from the IPO.
76669e66025171d1: KUALA LUMPUR: Overseas manufacturers selling cheap goods directly to Malaysian consumers through e-commerce platforms are putting local businesses at a disadvantage, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.

Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muda-Muar) said foreign manufacturers could undercut Malaysian businesses because they did not face the same operating costs and regulatory requirements as local companies.
These included taxes, minimum wage requirements and statutory contributions to the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) and Social Security Organisation (Socso), he said.

"Malaysian entrepreneurs are not asking for government handouts. They are not asking for competition to be shut down entirely. They only want fairness so they can compete on a level playing field," he said during the policy-stage debate on the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat.

Syed Saddiq proposed requiring foreign e-commerce operators to establish a local presence or collaborate with Malaysian businesses, saying this would also enable authorities to take action against defective or unsafe products.

He also urged the government to expedite its proposed e-commerce legislation to strengthen safeguards for local businesses, including requiring platforms to give advance notice before increasing fees and consult affected sellers.

He said the situation was compounded by rising charges imposed by major e-commerce platforms, including TikTok and Shopee, which he claimed had increased commission rates and other fees without sufficient notice.
"No prior notice, no prior warning," he said, warning that sudden increases could severely affect small businesses operating on thin profit margins.
Syed Saddiq described the situation as a "sandwich generation" problem for young entrepreneurs, who were being squeezed between cheap foreign competition and rising platform charges.
He warned that failure to address these pressures could force more small businesses to close despite improving economic indicators.
f33d7a4bf9478deb: KUALA LUMPUR: A shortage of medical officers at Sri Aman Hospital, Sarawak has raised concerns over staffing levels and patient safety in the district.
Reports claimed that only six of 20 scheduled officers had turned up on Sept 28.

Sri Aman member of parliament Datuk Seri Doris Sophia Brodi called on the Health Ministry to verify the figures and disclose how many medical officers had been offered placements, reported for duty or failed to report at hospitals and clinics in Sabah and Sarawak.
"At the Sri Aman Hospital, out of 20 scheduled medical officers, only six were reported present on September 28.

"I ask the ministry to verify this figure and state the actual number of medical officers offered placements, those who have reported for duty, and those who have not reported for duty at hospitals and clinics here," she said during the policy-stage debate on the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat.
She asked the ministry to outline immediate measures to address the shortage and prevent further strain on existing staff or compromise patient safety.

Separately, she also questioned the delay in approving the Sri Aman Integrated Health Complex, despite the issue having been raised repeatedly in the Dewan Rakyat and a technical report being submitted.

"How long do patients seeking treatment have to wait under temporary canopies, exposed to the heat, rain, and now the haze season, while doctors and staff are forced to work in increasingly stressful conditions?" she said.

Meanwhile, Doris welcomed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's announcement on permanent placements for contract doctors and increased incentives for nurses and paramedics, but called for a broader approach covering staffing, facilities, allowances and welfare particularly in remote areas.

Earlier, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said 337 of the 527 medical officers offered placements in Sarawak had reported for duty, compared with 336 of the 528 offered placements in Sabah.
To address the shortage, Dzulkefly said the ministry had taken several measures, including upgrading the ePlacement system to improve the permanent medical officer placement process.
c5103b0f53ee2761: HONG KONG: Hundreds of people queued in Hong Kong on Tuesday to view a Vincent van Gogh painting never publicly exhibited in more than six decades, ahead of a Sotheby's auction in New York where it is expected to fetch about US$180 million.
The Nov 18 auction will test the strength of the high-end art market, in which collectors have continued to compete for scarce trophy works, undeterred by broader economic uncertainty.

Painted in May 1890, "Chataigniers en fleurs", or "Chestnut Trees in Blossom", is one of the most important works from the Dutch artist's final days in the French village of Auvers-sur-Oise, where he died about two months later, aged 37.
The painting is poised to set a new auction record for a Van Gogh work, said Scott Niichel, of Sotheby's modern and contemporary art department in New York.
"This is a moment of extraordinary optimism, frenetic energy, enthusiasm, passion, and colour in the artist's body of work," he said.

Paintings from Van Gogh's final Auvers-sur-Oise period, just after his release from a psychiatric asylum in Saint-Remy-de-Provence, rarely come to market and the auction will draw the attention of collectors, museums and investors.

"I'd never heard of this painting before, so I wanted to see it with my own eyes," said Li Shanshan, a 50-year-old art lover who travelled about 2-1/2 hours from the southern city of Shenzhen to view the artwork.

The painting, which depicts a massive blossoming chestnut tree with a flowering canopy that dominates the composition, will be sold among part of a collection of 12 long-unseen works, including items by Paul Cezanne and Claude Monet.
Five unveiled at Sotheby's in London in late September included Cezanne's "Arlequin" and Monet's "Le Jardin des Tuileries."
After Van Gogh's death in July 1890, "Chataigniers en fleurs" was passed to his brother Theo, and then to the latter's widow Johanna van Gogh-Bonger and their son Vincent Willem.

Subsequently it was owned by German publisher Samuel Fischer, founder of S. Fischer Verlag, before entering the collection of George "Buddy" DeSylva, the American songwriter, film producer and co-founder of Capitol Records.

In 1953, the painting was acquired by collector Harriet Harris-Jonas, whose holdings were considered significant enough that New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art organised visits for patrons to view works in her Fifth Avenue apartment.
The painting was acquired by the Blaquier family from art dealer Wildenstein in 1975.
a4168b5f4753b4bc: KUALA LUMPUR: Equal allocations for members of parliament must be institutionalised to ensure fair treatment across the political divide, says Beluran MP Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee.
Debating in the Dewan Rakyat today, he said the move was necessary to guarantee equal funding regardless of which side of the House lawmakers sat on.
He said the issue had persisted since 2018, when opposition MPs were denied allocations by the government of the day.

"It wouldn't be wrong to appoint more than two Deputy Speakers. Indonesia has four Deputy Speakers.
"The Philippines has 14 Deputy Speakers for a House of Representatives of only 318 members.
"Thailand has two, Singapore has two, but our situation necessitates the appointment of additional Deputy Speakers," he said.

While acknowledging that appointing more Deputy Speakers would incur additional costs, including salaries, allowances, office space and staffing, he said the House needed more presiding officers to manage its sittings effectively.

3766f3a969b7133a: The UK Cabinet Office has scrapped a recruitment platform, recording a £7.8 million loss, while disclosing a potential penalty of up to £8.9 million over its handling of contractors' tax status. The department's annual report for 2025-26 said the Civil Service Jobs Applicant Tracking System (ATS) Programme, a central government plan for a unified, cross-departmental hiring system, was being closed to "align with the Shared Services for Government Strategy," which the Prime Minister's department also manages. The report said axing the program resulted in a "constructive loss" of £7.8 million. In March, a report from the National Audit Office said the ATS was an example of an interdependency that has not been effectively managed in the Shared Services Strategy, which is designed to bring Whitehall departments onto a common set of software-as-a-service (SaaS) enterprise applications. The Cabinet Office's annual report says closure will allow a new project better aligned with that strategy. "The program consistently identified lack of adoption from shared services clusters as a risk. At various points between 2023 and 2025, some shared services clusters raised concerns about the ATS program and stated that they would prefer to use the ATS functionality of their own ERPs over the new central platform. Despite this, Cabinet Office did not assess the need for a reset as soon as it could have, which made it challenging to assess alternative options for delivering an ATS. The ATS program was reset in October 2025," the report said. At the time, the Cabinet Office estimated that the total costs of the program reset would be £26 million to £38 million. The annual report estimates the Cabinet Office's liability for unpaid tax and National Insurance under IR35 off-payroll working rules, including interest, at £38.5 million. The rules affect many tech contractors working through their own companies. It paid £15 million toward settlement in February 2026, leaving a £23.5 million provision at year-end. The final settlement remains under negotiation. The department also disclosed potential HMRC penalties of up to £8.9 million, but considers payment unlikely because penalties can be suspended subject to compliance conditions. The report said: "The department has identified a remote contingent liability regarding potential financial penalties from HMRC relating to historic off-payroll working (IR35) compliance. In October 2025, HMRC concluded that the department's historic processes were inadequate and reasonable care was not taken, which can attract a penalty of 15 percent to 30 percent against the net tax liability before interest." Dave Chaplin, CEO of IR35 tax compliance firm IR35 Shield, said the HMRC assessment raises serious questions about compliance at the very heart of government. "The lesson for every organization engaging contractors is that claiming to take reasonable care is not the same as being able to demonstrate it. IR35 determinations must be supported by robust processes, accurate information, and evidence that the rules have been applied properly. Getting it wrong can have consequences far beyond the original tax bill," Chaplin said. ®
45ad9337ee37b95b: When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup this year, he didn’t think its data was worth much: the users were anonymous, the company just a few years old. But he’s since turned the firm’s digital archives into real money. He’s netted roughly $25,000 for his code base and a still-pending amount (likely around $15,000) for the workspace data in Google, Notion, Figma, and Slack. “At least all that stuff we were doing for two and a half years is worth something to someone somewhere,” he says.

The sale was brokered by a company called SimpleClosure, part of a new growth sector in tech: businesses catering to dying startups. Estimates from Carta and AngelList show shutdowns rising between 26% and 56% annually in recent years, and an end-of-life ecosystem—including coaches, “death doulas,” and firms that help handle the legal, tax, and operational headaches of going ­belly-up—has emerged. Now tech undertakers are selling the data remains to AI labs.

SimpleClosure added data sales to its services in April. Its Asset Hub platform helps founders sell their code and workspace data—emails, chats, documents. Buyers include foundation AI labs, vendors that construct simulated workspaces for AI training, and mature tech companies building their own models. Asset Hub has handled over 150 deals and expects to return over $10 million to startups by the end of 2026. CEO Dori Yona has seen these transactions, once rare and “somewhat taboo,” become increasingly routine, with 47% of SimpleClosure deals now including code or data sales.

And it’s got company. Industry rival Sunset also has a rapidly growing data resale business. Founder and CEO Brendan Mahony says Sunset values a dying client’s assets by head count, years in operation, volume of data, and how the team used its tools. Particle board, he says, is a good analogy: “This operational exhaust data is like the wood shavings that everyone thought had no value, but it actually has a ton.”

Demand for defunct companies’ data emerged suddenly last year, as AI training labs hit the limits of public and synthetic datasets. Surge AI, for example, buys data to build “reinforcement-learning gyms” where clients’ AI agents practice tasks—think debugging a complex IT architecture or drafting appellate briefs. Nick Heiner, who leads the company’s work on these environments, says he seeks data archives reflecting a range of situations, from disagreements to tricky judgment calls. Heiner explains that one company’s Slack history, if it captures conversations with variety and depth, can be worth more than another’s Slack, email, and calendars combined.

Real archives avoid common errors in synthetic worlds, such as references to dates that don’t exist, but the extent of performance gains remains unclear. No company has yet released tests comparing results of real-world data training with the alternatives. Pricing reflects this uncertainty: Buyers quote wildly different numbers, Heiner says, because valuations are based on “research theses” estimating how many useful tasks come from, say, 100,000 lines of code.

That hasn’t stopped bigger deals from happening. This past August, as part of Spirit Airlines’ bankruptcy, Google outbid the AI data company Mercor to buy the carrier’s decades of data, including 100 million emails, 500 million Teams messages, and 176,000 employee records. The price tag: $10 million. And Bloomberg reported in September that SpaceX’s AI unit is weighing buying data from struggling startups.

Legally, this all could get iffy. Spirit’s flight attendants’ union objected to the sale on privacy grounds, and Greg Ewing, an attorney who advises AI startups, has called such data “legally radioactive.” Suppliers employ data scientists to scrub personally identifiable information and exclude HR records, and buyers say they scrub too. But Ewing points out some of the private details that lurk in emails and calendars: doctor appointments, school pickup arrangements, date-night plans. He describes a “Wild West of AI training” that is only starting to give way to proper licensing agreements and vetted use.

There’s also the question of who profits from these windfalls. The proceeds typically flow to senior creditors and investors—not employees. To Ifeoma Ajunwa, a law professor at Emory University and author of The Quantified Worker, this represents a form of “captured capital.” Legal precedent allows for monitoring to help workers do their jobs, but once a firm is out of business, that justification vanishes. “Employers should have express consent before selling workers’ data,” says Ajunwa, but she adds that there’s no federal law banning such sales.

While many see this new market as a chance for failing businesses to recover some value, these wind-down sales also have limitations. Founders have little to no visibility into who is buying the data and what they plan to do with it. Plus, there’s little assurance they’re getting a fair offer. Data prices will likely stabilize in the coming year, though, unless an AI bubble pops first. Either way, tech’s new undertakers will be there to appraise what’s left.
Matthew King is a technology and environmental journalist based in Baltimore.
ef1dfac2164b99be: KUANTAN: Fisherman Mohd Faizal Abidin is facing an uncertain livelihood as the worsening haze is limiting his trips to sea, just weeks before the approaching monsoon season is expected to ground him ashore.

"I usually go out to sea about 5am and return around noon, but these days, I only leave about 8am. The poor air quality prevents us from travelling far or spending long hours at sea. ...I now venture only about 500 metres from the shoreline.

"Some fishermen who venture further offshore to cast their nets rely on global positioning system (GPS) devices to avoid getting lost in the poor visibility. Further out at sea, the haze resembles thick fog covering the surroundings," he told the New Straits Times.
Faizal said fishermen in Kuantan were racing against time to earn a living before the monsoon season, expected to begin next month, forces them to take on odd jobs to put food on the table.
"In the past, the year-end rainy weather was already a challenge for fishermen. Now, we have to deal with the haze just weeks before the monsoon season.
"Despite the haze, we still have to go to sea to earn a living," he said.

Meanwhile, fisherman Mohd Asri Abd Rahman, 54, said the community had little time left to make a living before the monsoon season arrives, adding that missing the opportunity to fish now would make the coming months even more difficult.
"The haze is unpredictable, and we only realise how thick it is after setting out to sea. Sometimes, we cannot see anything because everything appears white.
"The haze has worsened over the past few days. If it continues into next month, fishermen may have to take a longer break until the monsoon season ends next year before returning to sea," he said.
Kuantan Fishermen Association chairman Talib Husin advised fishermen to ensure their GPS devices were in good working condition before heading out to the South China Sea.
"Even when fishermen venture far offshore or encounter heavy haze, GPS devices can help guide them back to shore.

"Class A fishermen usually operate up to five nautical miles from the shoreline, but during hazy conditions, those with smaller boats tend to stay closer to shore," he said, adding that Kuantan had about 600 fishermen.

bbc6dd0e3355d4b0: TOKYO: Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi said on Tuesday that officials were reviewing the off-base code of conduct for US troops in Japan following the alleged killing of an Okinawan woman by a US Marine.

Crimes including rapes, assaults, hit-and-runs and drunk driving by US military personnel have long triggered protests on the southern Japanese island, which has for years urged other regions in the country to share the burden of hosting US troops.

"We plan to hold discussions including whether the existing rules are effectively functioning," Motegi said, adding that "matters such as patrols and curfew management" would be under review in talks with the United States.
The high-level bilateral consultations will examine off-duty conduct and the "liberty" policy governing off-base private activities of US military personnel, he said.

The existing policy, updated in 2024 following a string of sexual assaults by US military personnel in Okinawa, includes a ban on US military personnel drinking in public off base between 1 am and 5am or going to bars during those hours.
Japanese police arrested a US Marine stationed on Okinawa last week on suspicion of killing a 39-year-old woman at a hotel in the capital Naha.
The US military enacted a two-day operational pause after the Marine's arrest to reinforce discipline and standards, followed by a month-long curfew from midnight.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Tuesday that "we began high-level, working-level consultations between Japan and the United States last week on what effective measures should be taken."
"The Japanese government will continue to do everything in its power both to address this case and to ensure that it does not happen again," she told a legislative committee session.
Motegi held a telephone call at the weekend with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who offered his "sincere condolences" over the alleged crime, pledging US cooperation in the investigation.
Crimes committed by US personnel have been a thorn in relations between the close security allies.
Last year, a Japanese court sentenced a US Marine accused of choking and attempting to rape a woman in her 20s to seven years in prison.
The United States has around 54,000 military personnel stationed in Japan, mostly on Okinawa.

457f2327ba296fa0: CLEMENCE Remy moved to the French city of Nantes in 2020 and enrolled her two girls in the local state school.
The teachers were good, but she grew so exasperated by rolling staff strikes that she eventually put them in a private school.
Those concerns about state schools have helped fuel some of France's most violent protests in decades.

They began last month at high schools in Paris' poor northern suburbs, where anger over teacher absences and shabby facilities quickly morphed into a nationwide movement against inequality, weak public spending and falling standards.

France's public schools have long been held up as a crucible of the republican ideal, a place where children from rich and poor families alike can receive a top-notch education imbued with the values of "liberty, equality and fraternity."
But performance has been slipping for years, and the government is struggling to arrest the slide as gigantic pension outlays and a need to rein in public finances leave little room for manoeuvre.
Those issues have prompted a growing number of wealthier parents to abandon the public sector in favour of private schooling.
Remy said the strikes at her daughters' school in Nantes, a left-leaning city in western France, were often last-minute, requiring repeated time off work with little notice.
"School is an institution we should be able to rely on," she said. "In the end, you realise you can't rely on the system."

The maths and reading levels of French 15-year-olds have fallen drastically since 2003, reaching a record low well below the ‌Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development average, according to the body's 2025 "PISA" results.

French state secondary schools were unable to staff nearly 10 per cent of teaching hours - or almost half a day of teaching per week - in the 2024/25 school year, of which three-quarters is due to the non-replacement of absent teachers.

Between 10 and 20 per cent of French school buildings are "in a significantly deteriorated condition", according to a 2025 report by Banque des Territoires, the investment arm of state-owned lender Caisse des Depots.
The government's inability to turn the tide on education is partly explained by a growing pensions bill that sucks resources away from other priorities, experts say.
France's 2027 education budget is €64 billion (US$72 billion). Teachers' pensions add another 28 per cent to the cost.

Total government spending on pensions, which is due to reach 436 billion euros or 14 per cent of economic output next year, has grown faster than all other categories of public expenditure over the last two decades, while spending has slipped for education, according to Reuters calculations based on Eurostat data.
The steady growth in pension spending is due not only to an ageing population, but also to voters' resistance to increasing the retirement age or reducing what retirees get.
Economist Erwann Tison of the think tank Institut de l'Entreprise said pension spending "cannibalises" the education budget.
That means France can only pay early-career teachers below-OECD-average salaries that contribute to frustration and strike action.
"France is effectively handing over large subsidies to older French at the expense of everyone else," Nobel-winning economist Paul Krugman wrote on his Substack on Thursday.
"Mass national student demonstrations should come as no surprise."
The vast majority of French private schools operate according to the "under-contract" model.

Almost entirely Catholic-run, such schools have greater control over staffing and admissions. Their teachers are paid by the state, with fees covering non-teaching costs. A larger pool of substitute teachers means they are less affected by strikes or absences.
Over two million children, or 17.6 per cent of all pupils, attend one of France's more than 7,500 under-contract schools, according to a 2023 national audit office report.
Although this proportion rose modestly between 2011 and 2021, the percentage of children from wealthier families has grown at the expense of poorer children, the report found.
It said some families had moved over to avoid local state schools, or had concerns about safety and teacher absences.

Pupils from "very advantaged" families accounted for 40.2 per cent of the total in 2021 compared to just 26.4 per cent in 2000, while over half of pupils at under-contract schools now come from "advantaged or very advantaged" backgrounds, compared with less than a third in state schools.

"Fifty years ago, ambitious families aimed for the public sector," said Louis Chauvel, a sociologist at the University of Luxembourg. "Today, private institutions are often seen as the better route if you want to maximise your kids' chances."

Virginie Durin, the president of Apel, France's main association representing parents of pupils in Catholic private schools, said not all were wealthy, and that many parents made great sacrifices to afford them.
But she acknowledged a growing concentration of wealthier students in certain neighbourhoods.
Nantes, where Remy lives, is a stronghold of under-contract schools in France, with 38 per cent of pupils privately educated.
Remy, who pays €191 (US$214) a month per child, recognised that private schools were not affordable for everyone, and were at risk of being colonised by the wealthy. But she had no regrets.
"I think it provides an environment where at least the children are encouraged to strive and do better."

bd0573693b640d03: KUALA LUMPUR: The national track cycling squad is set to face its toughest assignment this year at the World Championships which begins at the Shanghai Velodrome on Chongming Island tomorrow.
The squad has had a busy year competing across the UCI World Cup Series, Tagaytay Asian Championships, Glasgow Commonwealth Games as well as the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
The world meet, however, is just as important as it also marks the start of the qualifying window for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
Former world keirin champion Azizulhasni Awang will again be Malaysia's best bet for a medal.

Despite his advancing years, the 38-year-old has been in the form of his life this season. He emerged as the overall keirin champion in the World Cup series after winning two keirin golds - he also won two individual sprint bronzes - and also won the keirin gold at both the Commonwealth and Asian Games.

The Netherlands' Harrie Lavreysen, who won four golds at last year's Santiago World Championships, and Australia's Matthew Richardson, who has made a comeback since suffering injuries during a crash in Japan just before the Commonwealth Games, will again be Azizulhasni's main rivals in the keirin.

Azizulhasni had beaten the duo in the World Cup series earlier this year but they will be at a different level of form when they compete at the worlds, especially with Olympic qualification points on the line.

Shah Firdaus Sahrom, who had yet to hit top form since undergoing knee surgery late last year, has not qualified to compete in any individual events in Shanghai but could play a role in the men's team sprint squad alongside his younger brother Ridwan, Fadhil Zonis and Akmal Jusena.
In the women's events, Izzah Izzati Asri and Nur Alyssa Farid will be looking to create an upset in the women's keirin though they will be facing European riders much faster than them.

The duo are, however, in good form having set a new national record en route to clinching the team sprint silver for Malaysia at the Asian Games alongside Aliana Azizan and Anis Amira Rosidi. Izzah also won keirin bronze at the Asiad.
National team head coach Harnizam Basri admitted that the squad is at a disadvantage when compared to their European rivals having had to compete at the Asian Games just a fortnight ago.

"The challenge for the squad is to try and maintain their performances as we have had to taper twice for the Commonwealth Games as well as the Asian Games in the lead-up to the world championships," he said recently.
"It is inevitable that they will lose some muscle mass due to the tapering though we will try our best to maintain our speed.
"For Azizulhasni, the big rivals for him will still be Harrie and Matthew.
"For the girls I would be happy to see them make it to the keirin semi-finals."
Azizulhasni, who took time away from the sport after Paris 2024, did not compete in the past two editions of the world championships.
The last time Malaysia won a medal at the world meet was during the 2020 Berlin edition when Azizulhasni won two bronzes via the keirin and men's individual sprint.
aacdf8aa8e3b5cbb: MANILA, Oct 13 — A Philippine impeachment court on Tuesday granted prosecutors’ request to drop two charges against Vice President Sara Duterte, including an alleged assassination threat against the president, leaving accusations of unexplained wealth as the sole remaining count against her.

cce2c1b3aebb895e: OCTOBER 13 — A visit to the emergency department often begins with urgency, triggered by a fall, stroke, heart attack, serious infection, or another acute medical condition requiring immediate clinical intervention. In these critical moments, the healthcare team’s primary objective is to manage the acute episode, deliver immediate treatment, and, when feasible, safely discharge the patient. However, an essential clinical and social question remains: what happens after discharge?

For many individuals, leaving the hospital door does not signal a return to their previous level of independent functioning. Patients frequently require ongoing assistance with fundamental activities of daily living, such as walking, bathing, eating, or administering medication. Others depend on structured rehabilitation, skilled nursing care, mobility equipment, physical home modifications, or continuous support from informal family caregivers. This critical gap between acute clinical stabilisation and sustained post-discharge functional survival defines the necessity of long-term care (LTC).

Long-term care refers broadly to ongoing assistance and support for individuals who experience difficulty living independently due to ageing, chronic illness, disability, or other health conditions. Unlike acute hospital treatment, which concentrates on resolving an immediate, short-term medical crisis, long-term care is extended in nature and may persist across months or even years. Understanding LTC as a multi-year post-acute necessity becomes critical when examined against Malaysia’s accelerating demographic projections.

Long-term care refers broadly to ongoing assistance and support for individuals who experience difficulty living independently due to ageing, chronic illness, disability, or other health conditions. — Busranu Aydin/Pexels pic
Demographic reality and healthy life expectancy gaps

Data from the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) underscores the rapid momentum of this demographic shift. The proportion of the Malaysian population aged 65 and above increased from 8.0 per cent in 2025 to 8.4 per cent in 2026, representing approximately 2.9 million people. Simultaneously, the population aged 60 and above reached roughly 4.2 million individuals, or 12.3 per cent of the total population. Actuarial projections indicate that Malaysia will officially transition into an ageing nation in 2036, when individuals aged 60 and above exceed 15 per cent of the total population.

Malaysians are undeniably achieving greater longevity. According to DOSM’s latest Abridged Life Tables, an infant born in 2026 has an average life expectancy at birth of 75.5 years. From the perspective of retirement and care planning, an individual reaching age 60 in 2026 is projected to live an additional 20.2 years on average — 18.9 years for males and 21.7 years for females.

However, a crucial actuarial distinction exists between total life expectancy and healthy life expectancy. World Health Organisation (WHO) data for Malaysia in 2021 indicates a Healthy Life Expectancy (HALE) at birth of 63.9 years, compared to an overall life expectancy at birth of 72.8 years. Because HALE takes into account the years lived in less than full health due to disease or injury, this statistical gap reveals a significant morbidity gap of 8.9 years spent in compromised health. Extended life expectancy without a parallel expansion in HALE results in a prolonged period of functional dependency, directly challenging healthcare risk models and the solvency assumptions of traditional retirement annuities. Consequently, population planning must evolve beyond asking, “How long might I live?” to confront the more crucial question: “How many of those years might I need assistance to live independently?”
The multi-dimensional burden: financial, practical, and familial

Consider the post-acute trajectory of an elderly patient presenting to the emergency department following a fall. While the acute physical injury may be successfully treated, the patient’s ongoing recovery extends far beyond the hospital ward. Post-discharge management frequently requires ongoing physiotherapy, home nursing services, specialised mobility equipment, adapted transportation, daily personal care assistance, or structural home modifications.

These long-term requirements impose direct financial liabilities and generate substantial indirect economic consequences for families. Spouses, adult daughters, or sons frequently adjust their professional obligations by reducing working hours, taking extended leave, or exiting the labour force entirely to serve as primary informal caregivers. The true financial footprint of long-term care extends well beyond immediate medical bills, directly eroding household earning capacity and workforce productivity.

Despite these catastrophic financial risks, traditional retirement planning relies heavily on income replacement models that assume static post-retirement consumption for basic living expenses—such as food, housing, daily overhead, and basic acute healthcare. Actuarially, long-term care does not follow a predictable, linear spending pattern; instead, it introduces asymmetric, catastrophic expenditure spikes in late life that can rapidly liquidate accumulated retirement reserves. Long-term care can no longer be treated as a peripheral contingency, but must be established as a distinct, dedicated pillar of retirement financial security.

Effective preparation for long-term care does not require predicting exact individual health trajectories. Rather, it demands systematic risk recognition and the pre-emptive alignment of multi-layered support frameworks prior to a health crisis. Essential pillars for long-term care readiness encompass personal liquid savings, tailored insurance or takaful protection mechanisms where appropriate, family financial resources, structured government support programmes, and community-based care networks.

When an unexpected medical emergency occurs, families are forced into immediate clinical decisions. However, the overarching challenge extends beyond acute hospitalisation costs: the immediate inquiry, “Can we afford today’s hospital treatment?” must be paired with the crucial long-term reality, “If the patient returns home but needs care for the next three, five or ten years, who will provide that care and how will we finance it?”

As Malaysia transitions toward an ageing society, funding for long-term care costs must be integrated into the core national conversation surrounding retirement policy, healthcare system sustainability, and social security infrastructure. Extended life expectancy is a major developmental achievement; ensuring that these added years are lived with physical dignity, structured support, and financial resilience represents an urgent national imperative.

* Associate Professor Dr Mazlynda Md Yusuf is an Actuarial Science and Risk Management Lecturer at Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia (USIM), and Dr Mohd Hafyzuddin Md Yusuf, is a Consultant Emergency Physician and Medical Lecturer at Universiti Malaya.

3ead45ba7fa00b79: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan sepatutnya meminda peraturan majlis mesyuarat Parlimen termasuk menggubal undang-undang peruntukan saksama selagi masih ada kuasa berbuat demikian, kata Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran).

Beliau menyeru peruntukan kawasan Parlimen saksama bagi semua Ahli Parlimen dijamin di bawah undang-undang, mempermudah akses bagi usul tidak percaya di Dewan Rakyat, serta meminda undang-undang antilompat parti.

Kiandee berkata, peruntukan kawasan Parlimen sepatutnya dilindungi undang-undang demi memastikan Ahli Parlimen pembangkang menerima dana sama seperti Ahli Parlimen kerajaan, tanpa mengira parti mana memegang kuasa.

Beliau mengakui Barisan Nasional (BN) telah gagal berbuat demikian sewaktu menjadi kerajaan, sekali gus menyebabkan Ahli Parlimennya tidak menerima peruntukan selepas gabungan itu hilang kuasa, pada PRU 2018.
"Nak menangis ketika itu, tak berair mata, kerana kita tidak jadikan itu undang-undang," katanya ketika perbahasan Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat.
"Jadi, bila anda ada kuasa, boleh lakukan ini, buat pindaan-pindaan tertentu supaya keadaan ini menjadi baik, tidak berlaku zaman dulu dan tidak berlaku lagi ke hadapan ini."
Beliau juga menggesa perubahan dilakukan terhaap peraturan majlis mesyuarat Parlimen bagi mengelak usul tidak percaya terhadap kerajaan diketepikan.

Berkait undang-undang antilompat parti, Kiandee berkata, ia gagal menghalang tindakan berpaling tadah politik, manakala pada masa sama mengenakan hukuman ke atas Ahli Parlimen seperti dirinya, yang digantung parti tetapi tidak dapat menyertai gabungan politik baharu.

"Maknanya, Akta Anti-Lompat bukan sahaja tidak berjaya menghalang melompat, tetapi menganiaya bagi kami yang dianiaya oleh parti," katanya merujuk kedudukannya sebagai naib presiden Bersatu yang digantung.

Kiandee mencadangkan kerajaan agar bertindak sebelum terlambat, sambil memberi amaran Ahli Parlimen kerajaan berkemungkinan menghadapi sekatan dan isu peruntukan yang sama suatu hari nanti sekiranya berlaku pertukaran kuasa.
"Kalau ada pertukaran kerajaan, mereka akan mengeluh seperti apa yang berlaku pada kami sekarang ini," katanya.
7bc11a6632fa8de8: KUALA LUMPUR: Proton Holdings Bhd is combining competitive servicing costs for the all new Saga and S70 with continued investment in aftersales support.

A five-year and 10-year study by Proton's after sales team highlights how competitive labour charges and complimentary labour benefits help keep scheduled servicing expenses manageable, reinforcing the value offered by its sedan range.
Proton claimed that the S70 records an estimated five-year scheduled maintenance cost of RM4,010.59.
Based on the study's summary comparison, this is about RM1,591 lower than the leading non-national B-segment competitor and RM433 lower than another rival that was recently launched.
The advantage extends to longer ownership periods.
Its estimated 10-year maintenance cost of RM9,070.09 represents savings of about RM2,191 and RM1,252 against both benchmark rivals.
The study also demonstrates competitive costs for the turbocharged S70.
Its estimated five-year maintenance cost is about RM1,076 below the first rival and is broadly comparable with the other, being only RM83 higher.
Over 10 years, its estimated maintenance cost is about RM1,575 and RM629 lower despite being a physically bigger vehicle offering a much higher level of driving performance.
Meanwhile, the all-new Saga offers estimated five-year scheduled maintenance costs starting from about RM3,357.
Both its four-speed automatic and CVT versions record lower five-year costs than the national brand benchmark used in the study, with savings of approximately RM174 and RM64 respectively.
The study covers scheduled maintenance items, prescribed replacements, labour charges and applicable taxes, based on 100,000km over five years and 200,000km over 10 years.
"As sales of Proton vehicles grow, our customers want to know their vehicle will remain affordable to maintain and that dependable support is within reach.
"Our focus is on combining competitive servicing costs with trained technicians, genuine parts and convenient access to our authorised network.
"Together, these help customers plan their maintenance spending and enjoy greater confidence throughout ownership," said after sales director Wan Hazran Wan Mustafa.
Proton's wider aftersales strategy complements its pricing approach by strengthening service accessibility and parts supply as its customer base grows.
Regional parts centres in Kuching and Kota Kinabalu support the distribution of aftersales parts and components across Sabah and Sarawak.
b1328e2f0826a97c: KUALA LUMPUR: Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman gesa rakyat memboikot syarikat terbabit pembakaran hutan sehingga menyebabkan jerebu rentas sempadan, dengan menggunakan kuasa membeli seperti pendekatan Dr Mahathir Mohamad ketika berdepan pertikaian dengan United Kingdom.

Beliau turut menggesa Malaysia mengemukakan bantahan diplomatik tegas kepada Indonesia serta mendapatkan sokongan negara Asean lain khususnya Singapura.
Katanya, kedua-dua negara juga boleh menggunakan pengaruh institusi kewangan masing-masing untuk menyekat pembiayaan kepada syarikat yang didapati terbabit pembakaran hutan.
Menurutnya, jerebu bukan sahaja menjejaskan pelancongan dan kesihatan awam, malah mengganggu pendidikan apabila sekolah terpaksa ditutup.

Syed Saddiq turut mencadangkan Malaysia mempertimbangkan undang-undang seumpama Akta Jerebu Rentas Sempadan Singapura bagi membolehkan tindakan diambil terhadap syarikat menyebabkan pencemaran merentasi sempadan.

31b2a20355e9b6d8: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Disruptions, unsafe encounters or legal ambiguities in the South China Sea could threaten Malaysia’s economic stability, national supply chains and regional food security, said Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah.

In his keynote address at the 9th Maritime Institute of Malaysia (Mima) South China Sea Conference 2026 here today, Hasbi stressed that maintaining freedom of navigation and unimpeded lawful commerce in these waters was a national imperative rather than an abstract legal principle.

“The South China Sea is the physical bridge connecting Peninsular Malaysia with Sabah and Sarawak. It sustains our domestic trade, powers our offshore energy sector and links our industries to global value chains,” he said.
Highlighting the nation’s reliance on maritime trade, Hasbi said more than 96.4 per cent of Malaysia’s total international trade was seaborne.

He said Malaysian ports handled 33.07 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in 2025, with Port Klang recording 15.14 million TEUs to rank as the world’s 10th-busiest container port in the Lloyd’s List One Hundred Ports 2026 ranking.
Meanwhile, Hasbi said the Port of Tanjung Pelepas handled 14.03 million TEUs, becoming the first single terminal in the country to surpass the 14-million-TEU threshold.
“This high level of connectivity also means that any disruption in the South China Sea instantly threatens our economic stability, national supply chains and regional food security,” he said.

Hasbi said conflicts in the Black Sea, Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz had shown how geopolitical tensions could disrupt maritime trade, increase freight and insurance costs, force vessels to take alternative routes and fuel inflation.

He also highlighted the risks posed by dark fleet or shadow fleet vessels, which engage in deceptive shipping practices such as illegal ship-to-ship transfers, disabling Automatic Identification Systems (AIS) and operating without valid insurance or meeting required safety standards.
“The lesson for our region is crystal clear: resilience cannot be reactive; it must be built proactively,” he said.

Hasbi also stressed that the Transport Ministry, together with the Marine Department Malaysia and the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA), had intensified vessel screening and maritime intelligence operations to detect and deter illicit shipping activities.

The measures include the use of advanced Vessel Traffic Services (VTS), International Maritime Organization (IMO) registration verification and integrated port database cross-checks, in line with IMO Resolution A.1192(33).
“We will not allow our waters or ports to become safe havens for non-compliant shipping activities that endanger innocent lives and our marine environment,” he said.

Reaffirming Malaysia’s position, Hasbi said disputes in the South China Sea should be resolved peacefully through dialogue, restraint and adherence to international law, including the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.

The 9th Mima South China Sea Conference 2026, themed “South China Sea 2026: Rules, Resilience, and Regional Order”, brings together policymakers, diplomats, academics, industry representatives and maritime experts to discuss regional maritime challenges and cooperation.

Also in attendance were representatives from the Australian High Commission, the Delegation of the European Union, the Embassy of Japan, the Embassy of the United States, the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China and the High Commission of Canada. — Bernama

The respective state education departments and individual school administrations have been urged to strictly monitor local air quality and immediately suspend all outdoor activities if conditions worsen.
Parents and school communities are advised to track official updates through the education ministry's portal and with the respective state departments.

889e738b8c468e66: PUTRAJAYA: Former Perak immigration prosecution chief Zaidi Dali began serving a three-year jail term today after the Court of Appeal restored his conviction on bribery charges.

Justice Noorin Badaruddin, who chaired a three-member bench, said the High Court judge had wrongly treated procedural deficiencies as fatal to the prosecution’s case rather than weighing the evidential value.
Justices Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid and Radzi Harun were the other members of the panel.

In her broad grounds, Noorin said the prosecution’s evidence had to be assessed cumulatively, taking into account the sequence of events surrounding a meeting on Nov 5, 2020, rather than viewing individual pieces of evidence in isolation.

She said Zaidi’s alleged role in soliciting RM10,000 a month to protect an entertainment centre from immigration inspections did not depend solely on whether he had personally uttered the words attributed to another participant.

The court also ruled that audio and video recordings relied on by the prosecution were admissible, as they were not intercepted communications requiring a certificate under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009.
It further found that the evidence concerning the RM7,000 bribe remained coherent despite the absence of an eyewitness to every movement of the money.
In 2022, the sessions court sentenced Zaidi and then Perak immigration director Zulhairin Yahya to three years’ imprisonment and fined each of them RM85,000.
The High Court in Ipoh acquitted both men last year. The prosecution appealed, but later withdrew its appeal against Zulhairin following his death earlier this year.
The men had been accused of conspiring to protect an entertainment centre in Manjung from enforcement raids in exchange for monthly payments of RM10,000.
M Athimulan and R Vikramanan represented Zaidi, while deputy public prosecutors Farah Ezlin Yusop Khan, Maziyah Mansor and Qistini Qamarul Abrar appeared for the prosecution.
a61bb1643620510d: MELBOURNE, Oct 13 — Emergency departments at Australian hospitals are unprepared for the country’s ageing population, a report has warned, according to Xinhua.

The report released on Tuesday by the Australasian College for Emergency Medicine (ACEM) said almost nine million people sought care at emergency departments nationwide in 2023-24, a quarter of whom were aged 65 and over.

Within that age group, more than half arrived at hospital by ambulance, almost 70 per cent needed urgent care and 50 per cent were admitted to a hospital bed, compared with less than a quarter of younger patients.

It said 53,510 older patients spent longer than 24 hours in emergency departments awaiting a hospital bed in 2023-24, up 254 per cent from 15,084 in 2018-19, while only 54 per cent of older patients who needed admission left the emergency department within the eight-hour target.

A landmark intergenerational report released by the federal Treasury in September projected that the proportion of Australia’s population aged 65 and over would grow from 17.8 per cent currently to 24.8 per cent by 2066.
The ACEM report projected that emergency department arrivals among people aged 85 and over would increase by 411 per cent by 2050.
“Our health system and its workforce are just not equipped for this demographic change,” ACEM president Peter Allely said in a media release.
“Unless these serious issues are addressed as a matter of urgency, emergency care will come too late for many Australians.”

The report made several recommendations to federal, state and territory governments, including improving integration between hospitals and aged care, increasing funding and rapidly expanding the residential aged care sector. — Bernama-Xinhua

5ee58683ed0f54bf: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 13 — Police believe an early morning arson attack targeting several homes at an ethnic Rohingya settlement in Kulai Besar was triggered by racially provocative videos circulating on social media.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad confirmed that Molotov cocktails were hurled at the settlement, likely sparking localised fires along the perimeter fences of several residences.
“However, the fire was successfully extinguished and there were no injuries or other damage reported.
“Police have also received a report on the incident at 1.30am,” he said in a statement today.
Initial investigations indicate the attack could have been retaliation by individuals angered by two viral video clips circulating online.
Ab Rahaman said the footage showed a group of ethnic Rohingya youths issuing challenges for a street confrontation in the Kulai area.
“The individuals in the video also claimed that the Malay community lacked the courage to enter the area,” he said, adding that police also received a report on the videos.

In a related development, a Rohingya man in his 30s lodged a separate police report denying any involvement in the viral content, claiming that unidentified individuals had appropriated his photograph without consent to manufacture the provocative videos.
Ab Rahaman said police have launched investigations under both anti-arson statutes and cyber-crime laws.
“Police have opened two investigation papers regarding this incident. Investigators are probing the case under Section 436 of the Penal Code for mischief by fire or explosive substances.
“Police are also investigating the case under Sections 505(b) and 505(c) of the Penal Code that deal with statements, rumors, or reports that cause public mischief, fear, or communal incitement.
“The case is also being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 regarding the improper use of network facilities,” he said.

The incident highlights escalating communal friction in Malaysia, where public and political attitudes toward the displaced Rohingya community have increasingly hardened from initial humanitarian sympathy to visible resentment.
Such hostility is frequently fuelled by online misinformation, unverified social media narratives, and localised discontent with suburban migrant enclaves.
Malaysia is not a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention, but currently hosts more than 126,000 registered Rohingya refugees through the UNHCR.
