b9e41dc302aadd49: COLOMBO: Sri Lanka's fragile recovery from its worst economic crisis in decades could be undermined by the country's worst-ever El Nino conditions, the central bank has warned.

The Central Bank of Sri Lanka also said last year's Cyclone Ditwah, which killed some 650 people and caused billions in damage, had weakened asset values and increased risks for lenders as the island emerges from its 2022 sovereign default.

"Climate-related risks, such as the El Nino phenomenon, and elevated volatility in financial markets created a challenging external environment, with potential implications for domestic macroeconomic and financial stability," the bank said in a report published late Monday.
The World Bank has estimated infrastructure losses from the cyclone at around US$4.1 billion, while the government has launched a US$1.6 billion recovery programme.
Sri Lanka is recovering from an unprecedented economic meltdown that culminated in its first sovereign default in April 2022 after it ran out of foreign exchange to pay for essential imports.
Shortages of food, fuel and medicines triggered months of protests that forced then-president Gotabaya Rajapaksa from office.
After securing a US$2.9 billion IMF bailout in March 2023, Colombo restructured its foreign debt and returned to growth, with the World Bank saying the economy has recovered to pre-crisis levels.
But the central bank warned that worsening weather linked to El Nino could create fresh strains on households and businesses, hurting banks through rising loan defaults.

Sri Lanka's Meteorological Department has forecast torrential rains through December followed by a prolonged drought early next year, describing the current El Nino episode as the worst the country has experienced.
"The current El Nino-related weather conditions would exert pressure on financial institutions through a deterioration in credit quality," the report said.
El Nino is a naturally occurring climate pattern associated with warmer ocean temperatures in the Pacific that can change wind and rainfall patterns around the world.
Scientists say human-caused climate change can amplify its effects by making more energy and moisture available to fuel extreme weather.
82620b3ccd61c8e6: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should amend parliamentary rules while it still has the power to do so, says Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran).
He called for equal constituency allocations for all MPs to be guaranteed by law, easier access to no-confidence motions in the Dewan Rakyat, and amendments to the anti-hopping law.
Kiandee said constituency allocations should be protected by law to ensure opposition MPs receive the same funding as government MPs, regardless of which party is in power.
He admitted that Barisan Nasional had failed to do this when it was in government, leaving its MPs without allocations after the coalition lost power in the 2018 general election.
“We wanted to cry then, but it was our own fault for not making it the law,” he said during the debate on the 2027 budget in the Dewan Rakyat.
“While you are still in office and have the power, you can make certain amendments to improve the situation. This will ensure that what happened in the past does not happen again.”
He also called for changes to parliamentary rules to prevent no-confidence motions against the government from being sidelined.

On the anti-hopping law, Kiandee said it had failed to stop political defections while penalising MPs such as himself, who had been suspended by their parties but were unable to pursue new political alliances.
“The anti-hopping law has not stopped defections, but it has punished those of us who have been mistreated by our parties,” said the suspended Bersatu vice-president.
Kiandee urged the government to act before it was too late, warning that its MPs could one day face the same restrictions and funding issues if political power changed hands.
“If there is a change of government, they will complain just as we are complaining now,” he said.
a80353a8e8e46c3b: If you're encountering some odd IPv6 networking issues, the culprit might be the Intel Connectivity Performance Suite (ICPS), although the chipmaker has kept quiet about the problem. A Samsung Galaxy Book owner contacted The Register about some decidedly odd networking behavior that they eventually traced to unwanted ICPS optimizations. And by "optimization", we mean "borked networking." For our reader, the problem showed up in OneDrive and OneNote. Notebooks were showing as empty, even though they were reported as "Up to date" according to the software. Microsoft couldn't get to the bottom of it. A bit of sleuthing by our reader revealed that something was borking the IPv6 packet. Removing Samsung's ICPS build (40.25.926.0) and installing the generic release (50.26.623.243) fixed the problem. Our reader told us, "From the user's side it looks like random 'connection reset' errors on all kinds of sites, plus OneNote saying 'We can't get to your notebooks right now.' "IPv4 is unaffected, which is why the web version and my phone kept working and nobody could figure out what was going on." It isn't only Samsung and our reader affected. Intel's own Community forums shows other users encountering the same glitch. An ASUS user put together an exhaustive report on the issue (IPv6 connection woes while IPv4 worked well). In this instance, ICPS version 40.25.725.165 was in use, and the problem went away following uninstallation. The user asked whether there was an official way to opt out of ICPS permanently, and the Intel Customer Support Technician responded: "Good news!… We can confirm that the Wireless driver and ICPS are available as separate standalone driver packages." So in that particular instance, ditching ICPS would make no difference. Which, of course, raises another question – in this example (where the Intel BE201 Wi-Fi adaptor is present), why is it even there? The answer: "It is often bundled with OEM systems as an added value software to enhance the overall wireless experience." You might see "enhance," but for users affected by IPv6 problems, it's more like "break." The issue is insidious, and broken ICPS builds are still floating around, ready to catch users off guard. According to our reader, Microsoft's own Update Catalog will hand out the broken drivers, which effectively break Microsoft 365 services on certain hardware. For the ASUS user, the issue affected Chrome, Edge, and Windows curl.exe. "Approximately 40–60 percent of IPv6 HTTPS connections to an AWS CloudFront distribution were reset. IPv4 was completely stable." According to our reader, "Intel created the bug, then fixed it quietly." Updating to the later, generic version appears to fix things. However, according to the Intel technician, as of the July post, "we do not have a confirmed public advisory for this specific behavior." We asked Intel and Microsoft for comment, but neither responded. However, judging by forum comments, the issue has caught out plenty of users. As such, if you find yourself with some weird networking issues with IPv6 and are using ICPS (as many will be), it might be worthwhile checking out the generic rather than OEM version of the software or removing it altogether to see if the problem goes away. ®
49fbac37dc926a54: NEW DELHI, Oct 13 — India’s youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) said on Tuesday that key leaders had been detained after entering an iconic protest site in New Delhi that was blocked by police.

Opposition parties and supporters of the movement have taken to the streets in recent days, defying a security clampdown to demand the resignation of the head of India’s Election Commission, accusing it of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party.
The Election Commission of India, which oversees the voting process in the world’s most populous nation, has denied any wrongdoing.
Delhi Police said on Monday that Jantar Mantar in the heart of the capital had been taken off the list of designated official protest sites.
The site has been sealed off for several days by yellow metal barricades and guarded by a heavy police presence.

But a video posted online by CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday showed protesters clambering over the barricades, running into the empty space and waving the national flag — before police chased and detained them.
“CJP sneaks inside to reclaim Jantar Mantar,” the group said in a post on social media, adding that those detained included leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde.
“All of them have been detained by Delhi Police,” it added.

Delhi Police had announced three official sites on Monday as alternatives to Jantar Mantar, where protesters have gathered for decades — including CJP demonstrations that led to the education minister stepping down over an examination scandal in July.
“You cannot denotify the resistance,” Dipke said, tagging Modi in his post.
Modi, in comments at a business conference in New Delhi on Tuesday, called India the “mother of democracy”, but did not refer directly to the protests.
“In our country, people openly debate a wide range of issues and discuss different perspectives,” he said. — AFP
89720bf45fb86292: PETALING JAYA: Civil society groups have called for earlier announcements and clearer guidelines on haze-related school closures.

Melaka Action Group for Parents in Education (Magpie) proposed that the education ministry announce the next day's school arrangements by noon on the preceding day, instead of waiting until the evening.

"While we recognise that haze conditions can change rapidly and urgent announcements may sometimes be unavoidable, earlier communication should be the standard practice whenever circumstances permit," it said in a statement.
Magpie said earlier notice would help parents arrange childcare and transport while giving teachers time to prepare lessons and alternative learning plans.
"A more predictable announcement system would help all stakeholders prepare responsibly, without compromising the health and safety of our children," it said.
Education minister Fadhlina Sidek had defended the day-to-day approach to school closures, saying that closure decisions must account for changing air quality and the impact on students’ learning.
She also explained that haze management involved several agencies, with the environment department responsible for air quality and the health ministry providing guidance on health risks.
The education ministry, meanwhile, focussed on students’ safety and the management of school operations based on prevailing conditions, she said.
State education directors have also been tasked with announcing school operational decisions based on air pollutant index (API) readings and the ministry's guidelines.
School closures must be announced by 2.45pm on Saturdays for Group A schools and Sundays for Group B schools, and by 5.45pm on other days, based on the API readings.
Group A schools are those with a Friday-Saturday weekend, and Group B with a Saturday-Sunday weekend.
However, Engage and Projek SAMA questioned the differing API thresholds and closure decisions during the recent haze episode in Johor, including the statewide closure of schools for two days.
“Together, they have produced uncertainty over a basic question: who is authorised to make the final decision, using what criteria, and with what notice?” they asked in a joint statement.
They said sudden closures could force parents who failed to arrange childcare to miss work, while lower-income families might not have suitable conditions to keep their children indoors safely.
"A closure policy must, therefore, be accompanied by practical support, not simply an instruction to stay home," they said.

As such, Engage and Projek SAMA called for school closure decisions to be based on transparent, science-based criteria that took into account air quality readings, exposure duration, weather forecasts, indoor air conditions and health risks.
They also urged the government to establish a permanent National Haze Operations Room, or an equivalent coordinating body, to bring together relevant ministries, agencies and state governments.
48e61c5396d04c9d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Miri residents will have another air travel option when a new flight service to Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport (LTSAAS) in Subang begins operations on December 1, 2026.
Deputy Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Chiew Choon Man said the new route would benefit residents who frequently travel for work, business, education, medical treatment and family commitments.
He said Subang Airport’s proximity to central Kuala Lumpur and surrounding areas would offer greater convenience to travellers, particularly in terms of accessibility and onward land transportation.

“I welcome this announcement because the addition of this route is not just about providing more flight options, but also about enhancing Miri’s connectivity with the country’s main economic centres,” he said in a statement today.

Chiew, who is also the Miri Member of Parliament, said he had previously met with Batik Air to discuss the possibility of introducing the route and welcomed the positive developments leading towards its implementation.
He said improved air connectivity could benefit the business and tourism sectors while making travel between Miri and the Klang Valley more convenient.

“I believe better air transport links are important for a city like Miri, which has tremendous potential for further growth. More flight options mean greater convenience for residents and more opportunities to stimulate local economic activity,” he said. — Bernama
976aa7d73259e225: PUTRAJAYA: Semua sekolah di Johor, Melaka, dan Negeri Sembilan ditutup esok susulan jerebu melanda negara.

ba7f909014c37d2f: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living is “actively” working on a dedicated legal framework to combat ticket scalping, with new regulations expected to take effect as early as next year, Parliament was told this morning.

Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said anti-scalping provisions could be inserted under Section 15(1) of the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act, which grants authority to introduce measures curbing unfair pricing and resale practices.

“The ministry is currently engaging in engagement sessions with event organisers and conducting benchmarking studies with the objective and intention of establishing a legal framework,” he said during Question Time.

“Under Act 723, or the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act, Section 15(1) provides the minister and the Ministry the power to establish a mechanism in the form of regulations that we can use to curb these scalping activities,” he added.

Scalping is a term used to describe the practice of buying something highly sought after like concert tickets, shoes, or clothing and then reselling it at a much higher price, leveraging scarcity and demand.

While scalping in Malaysia has been around for some time, backlash against the practice blew up when British rock giants Coldplay came to perform in Kuala Lumpur in 2023, when scalpers bought tickets in big numbers and then resell them at exorbitant rates.
For example, the standard CAT 1 tickets that were originally priced at RM1,288 were re-listed for reportedly up to RM43,000, sparking outrage.

Investigative reports suggest scalping in Malaysia has evolved from individuals reselling a few extra tickets into an organised, tech-driven operation affecting multiple sectors as scalpers began utilising internet bots to make bulk purchases.
Bots help resellers bypass virtual waiting rooms to buy bulk batches of tickets within seconds before human buyers even load the payment page.

Armizan said the anti-scalping provisions would include the definition of scalping itself, how to control bulk ticket purchasing activities and enforcing the use identification or names on ticket purchases.
“Because when bulk ticket purchases happen — whether through bots or by individuals — this is where secondary sales or a secondary layer of sales occur,” he said.
“So that is where the situation of scalping may arise. This is what we are studying.”
622b101cbd13ac5d: PETALING JAYA: Pengerusi Pakatan Harapan (PH) Sabah Mustapha Sakmud mencabar Ketua Pembangkang Hamzah Zainudin mengemukakan belanjawan alternatif yang memperincikan cara mengurangkan defisit fiskal tanpa menjejaskan pembangunan negara.

Cabaran itu susulan kritikan Hamzah terhadap Belanjawan 2027, yang menurutnya berisiko membebankan institusi strategik negara seperti Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) dan Kumpulan Wang Persaraan (Diperbadankan) (KWAP) dengan keputusan kerajaan.

“Ketua pembangkang sewajarnya mengemukakan cadangan belanjawan alternatif yang jelas dan terperinci, termasuk bagaimana beliau mahu mengurangkan defisit fiskal sambil memastikan pembangunan negara, khususnya di Sabah dan Sarawak terus dilaksanakan,” katanya dalam kenyataan.
Mustapha berkata, penurunan defisit fiskal menunjukkan kerajaan berusaha mengurus kewangan negara secara berhemah bagi mengurangkan beban hutang yang perlu ditanggung generasi akan datang.

“Angka tidak berbohong. Defisit fiskal negara pernah mencecah 6.4% KDNK pada 2021 dan 5.5% pada 2022. Namun, sejak pentadbiran kerajaan, defisit terus menurun daripada 5.0% pada 2023 kepada 4.1% pada 2024 dan 3.7% pada 2025,” katanya.

Beliau berkata, defisit fiskal diunjurkan terus berkurang kepada 3.6% tahun ini dan 3.3% pada 2027, manakala pinjaman baharu kerajaan persekutuan menurun daripada kira-kira RM100 bilion setahun pada 2021 dan 2022 kepada RM75.6 bilion pada 2025.

Katanya, Belanjawan 2027 turut memperuntukkan RM18.7 bilion kepada Sabah dan RM16.2 bilion kepada Sarawak, menjadikan jumlah peruntukan kepada kedua-dua negeri itu RM34.9 bilion, meningkat RM2.2 bilion berbanding tahun sebelumnya.
“Inilah bukti disiplin fiskal tidak menghalang kerajaan daripada terus melaksanakan agenda pembangunan negara,” katanya.
50d1a6762af101d7: HONG KONG: Hundreds of people queued in Hong Kong on Tuesday to view a Vincent van Gogh painting never publicly exhibited in more than six decades, ahead of a Sotheby's auction in New York where it is expected to fetch about US$180 million.
The Nov 18 auction will test the strength of the high-end art market, in which collectors have continued to compete for scarce trophy works, undeterred by broader economic uncertainty.

Painted in May 1890, "Châtaigniers en fleurs", or "Chestnut Trees in Blossom", is one of the most important works from the Dutch artist's final days in the French village of Auvers-sur-Oise, where he died about two months later, aged 37.
The painting is poised to set a new auction record for a Van Gogh work, said Scott Niichel, of Sotheby's modern and contemporary art department in New York.
"This is a moment of extraordinary optimism, frenetic energy, enthusiasm, passion, and colour in the artist's body of work," he said.

Paintings from Van Gogh's final Auvers-sur-Oise period, just after his release from a psychiatric asylum in Saint-Remy-de-Provence, rarely come to market and the auction will draw the attention of collectors, museums and investors.

"I'd never heard of this painting before, so I wanted to see it with my own eyes," said Li Shanshan, a 50-year-old art lover who travelled about 2-1/2 hours from the southern city of Shenzhen to view the artwork.

The painting, which depicts a massive blossoming chestnut tree with a flowering canopy that dominates the composition, will be sold among part of a collection of 12 long-unseen works, including items by Paul Cezanne and Claude Monet.
Five unveiled at Sotheby's in London in late September included Cezanne's "Arlequin" and Monet’s "Le Jardin des Tuileries".
After Van Gogh's death in July 1890, "Châtaigniers en fleurs" was passed to his brother Theo, and then to the latter's widow Johanna van Gogh-Bonger and their son Vincent Willem.

Subsequently it was owned by German publisher Samuel Fischer, founder of S. Fischer Verlag, before entering the collection of George "Buddy" DeSylva, the American songwriter, film producer and co-founder of Capitol Records.

In 1953, the painting was acquired by collector Harriet Harris-Jonas, whose holdings were considered significant enough that New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art organised visits for patrons to view works in her Fifth Avenue apartment.
The painting was acquired by the Blaquier family from art dealer Wildenstein in 1975.
573f2833b32f42b1: JAKARTA, Oct 13 — Indonesia’s Mount Semeru in East Java erupted at least 10 times on Tuesday, sending volcanic ash up to 900 metres above its summit.
According to the Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation Centre (PVMBG), the eruptions occurred between 12.09am and 1.11pm local time, with ash clouds drifting southwest and west.
Based on a report on its official website, the highest ash columns, reaching 900 metres above the summit or 4,576 metres above sea level, were recorded during eruptions at 5.20am and 6.47am.

With Mount Semeru remaining at Level III, the second-highest level on Indonesia’s four-tier volcanic alert system, PVMBG advised the public to avoid all activities within 13 kilometres of the summit along the Besuk Kobokan River in the volcano’s southeastern sector due to the risk of pyroclastic flows and volcanic mudflows.
“People must also avoid all activities within a five-kilometre radius of Mount Semeru’s crater or summit due to the danger of ejected incandescent rocks,” it said.

The report noted that the volcano, located on the border of Lumajang and Malang regencies in East Java, also erupted five times between 12.09am and 5.13am, producing ash columns ranging from 300 to 800 metres, followed by two eruptions at 8.10am and 10.37am that sent ash 800 metres above the summit.

It said the latest reported eruption at 1.11pm produced a 600-metre ash column drifting southwest, with seismic instruments recording a maximum amplitude of 15 millimetres and a duration of 88 seconds. — Bernama

d483836d93c2466a: SHAH ALAM: A lorry driver pleaded not guilty in the magistrates' court here to driving against traffic while under the influence of drugs and causing injuries to four individuals last week.
C Agilan, 51, entered the plea after the charge against him was read out before magistrate Ameera Mastura Khamis.

Agilan is accused of driving a lorry while under the influence of methamphetamine and amphetamine, rendering him unable to control the vehicle and resulting in injuries to four people aged between 58 and 17.
He was charged with committing the offence at about 4.30pm on Oct 9 on Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari.
He was charged under Section 44(1A)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which provides for a maximum jail term of 10 years and a maximum fine of RM50,000.
Deputy public prosecutor Alia Anisa Khairus Masnan proposed bail of RM15,000.
Agilan’s lawyer Rohan Singh requested a minimum bail amount, saying his client had to support his unemployed wife and an 11-year-old child on a salary of about RM1,700 a month.
In a separate court before magistrate Wan Noora Nisa Ngadirin, Agilan pleaded not guilty to a charge of self-administering methamphetamine and amphetamine.
The charge was framed under Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, which carries a jail term of up to two years, or a fine of up to RM5,000, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Amirah Zahari proposed bail of RM7,000, after which Rohan requested a minimum bail amount.
For the first charge, the court granted bail of RM9,000 and suspended his driving licence until the case is concluded, while for the second, he was allowed bail of RM3,900.
The cases are set for mention on Dec 22 this year and Jan 11, 2027, respectively.
115e2f4952db8627: TOKYO: Japanese foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi said on Tuesday that officials were reviewing the off-base code of conduct for US troops in Japan following the alleged killing of an Okinawan woman by a US Marine.

"We plan to hold discussions, including whether the existing rules are effectively functioning," said Motegi, adding that "matters such as patrols and curfew management" would be under review in the talks with the US.
The high-level bilateral consultations will examine off-duty conduct and the "liberty" policy governing off-base private activities of US military personnel, he said.

The existing policy, updated in 2024 following a string of sexual assaults by US military personnel in Okinawa, includes a ban on US military personnel drinking in public off-base between 1am and 5am or even going to bars during those hours.
Japanese police arrested a US Marine stationed on Okinawa last week on suspicion of killing a 39-year-old woman at a hotel in the capital Naha and stealing her wallet.
The US military enacted a two-day operational pause after the Marine's arrest to reinforce discipline and standards, followed by a month-long curfew from midnight.
Motegi held a telephone call at the weekend with US secretary of state Marco Rubio, who offered his "sincere condolences" over the alleged crime, pledging US cooperation in the investigation.
cfee0fe2b4a82ae0: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Malaysia continues to enjoy tariff exemptions for its semiconductor exports to the United States, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister (Miti) Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
He emphasised that Malaysia has yet to receive any indication that Washington will impose tariffs on the sector’s exports.

“We have not received any indication that the US will impose tariffs on Malaysian semiconductors at this time,” said Johari in a press conference at the European Union-Malaysia Business Day 2026: Selangor in Focus here today.
He said negotiations with the US under Section 301 covered four issues, namely forced labour, excess production capacity, the environmental standards and government subsidies.
“Environment and state subsidies, we are fine. We are not subject to anything because we are clear.
“The forced labour issue has been finalised, with Malaysia subject to a 10 per cent rate, compared with 12.5 per cent for other countries. Only 17 economies have been charged 10 per cent.
“The only thing that is not finalised is excess capacity. We do not have excess capacity,” said Johari.

He said that any excess capacity associated with goods exported from Malaysia could be from third countries, adding that Malaysia would seek clarification from the US on the countries identified as contributing to the issue.

“That (excess capacity) is from a third country. We will commit (but) they must give us a list that they assume is a country that is subject to excess capacity. Then we will take them out from our list,” said Johari.
He said access to overseas markets depended on meeting the respective countries’ requirements and regulations.

“At the end of the day, any market that you want to go to is up to them. What are their criteria? What is the law that we need to comply with? Then we need to comply; otherwise you cannot go,” he said.
Johari said the EU imposed strict environmental requirements on its trading partners.
“As long as you can comply, then that is it. Likewise, I think any other country does not matter. Everyone has a unique requirement,” he said.
The EU-Malaysia Business Day 2026: Selangor in Focus was held in conjunction with the Selangor International Business Summit (SIBS), scheduled from October 14 to 17, 2026.

Hosted by the Delegation of the European Union to Malaysia, the third edition of the annual flagship event was organised in collaboration with the Selangor state government, Invest Selangor and Eurocham Malaysia.

Held under the theme “Bridging Innovation-Powering Progress”, the event aimed to advance business ties and further unlock investment opportunities involving the substantial EU business presence in Malaysia.

With over 550 EU companies operating in Selangor, generating a total annual revenue of over RM51 billion, the event highlights high-growth and high-value sectors such as advanced manufacturing, green transition, digitalisation and logistics.
Also present were EU Commissioner for International Partnerships, Jozef Sikela, and Ambassador of the EU to Malaysia, Rafael Daerr.
Sikela said that investing alongside Malaysia would strengthen and diversify the semiconductor ecosystem on which both economies increasingly depend.

“We live in a world of geopolitical tensions, economic disruptions and growing competition over critical technologies in the world, which is becoming more and more like a world where controversial and resilient supply chains and trusted, mutually beneficial partnerships matter more than ever,” he said.

Sikela said the resumption of negotiations on the Malaysia-EU Free Trade Agreement (MEUFTA) would further deepen economic ties, citing Lumut Maritime Industrial City as another potential area for collaboration.

“The Lumut Maritime Industrial City is another good example of opportunities ahead, bringing together infrastructure, industry, logistics and potential for greener maritime activities,” he said. — Bernama
b977dc560a7afdf2: PETALING JAYA: Kerusi dimenangi Pakatan Harapan (PH) pada pilihan raya lalu akan kekal ditandingi parti penyandang termasuk Ayer Keroh dimenangi DAP, kata Azman Abidin.
Setiausaha politik kepada perdana menteri berkata, persetujuan itu dicapai dalam perbincangan pimpinan PH Melaka, sekali gus menafikan dakwaan PKR akan mengambil alih kerusi DAP.

“Mungkin laporan media yang memetik PKR akan bertanding di Ayer Keroh itu berdasarkan salah faham. Kenyataan mengenai DUN Ayer Keroh merujuk kepada bakal ditandingi komponen PH, bukannya PKR secara khusus,” katanya kepada FMT.

Beliau turut menegaskan hubungan antara parti komponen PH kekal harmoni dan semua parti akan bergerak sebagai satu pasukan menghadapi PRN Melaka.

ae4df67aef90a1c9: KUALA LUMPUR: The domestic trade and cost of living ministry is studying Section 15(1) of the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011 (Act 723) to determine how it can develop a framework to combat ticket scalping, deputy minister Fuziah Salleh said today.
She said the review was also looking at laws in other countries to identify the best approach suited to Malaysia’s needs.
“The study is examining laws in countries such as Australia, Ireland, Canada, Japan, Taiwan and Singapore,” she told the Dewan Rakyat.

According to Section 15(1) of Act 723, the minister shall “prescribe the mechanism to determine that profit is unreasonably high, and different types of mechanisms may be prescribed to cater for different conditions and circumstances as the minister deems fit”.
Fuziah said the proposed legislation, targeted for implementation by next year, aims to define scalping and regulate bulk online ticket purchases.
“When tickets are bought in bulk, whether through bots or individuals, it can lead to secondary sales and scalping.
“We will also study the possibility of verifying buyers’ and ticket holders’ identities, as well as the suitability of existing price control and anti-profiteering provisions,” she said.
Fuziah was replying to Isam Isa (BN-Tampin), who asked about efforts to formulate legislation to tackle ticket scalping.
She said her ministry was also examining enforcement challenges to ensure the legislation accounts for different types of ticket transactions, particularly for one-off events.
Fuziah said her ministry would step up consumer advocacy and engage event organisers to promote more transparent ticket sales, including clearer purchase terms and conditions.
41eb15d228d1639c: BEIJING: US payments firm Visa has received approval from China's central bank to begin preparations for a domestic bank card clearing institution in the country, ending years of waiting to tap into one of the world's largest payment markets.

The move marks a major step for Visa to join rivals American Express and Mastercard in operating bank card clearing services in China and represents a further opening up of the nation's tightly controlled financial sector.
The People's Bank of China (PBOC) issued an administrative approval to Visa Information Technology (Beijing) Co Ltd permitting it to begin preparatory work, according to the central bank's website.
Visa Information Technology (Beijing) is a foreign-invested enterprise established in China by Visa.
"The approval of our Application to Prepare marks a significant step forward in Visa's long-standing commitment to China," Visa CEO Ryan McInerney said in a statement on Tuesday.

The approval comes after US President Donald Trump's summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping earlier this year in China, which included more than a dozen CEOs of top US companies, including those of Mastercard and Visa.
"We greatly appreciate the important role of the leaders of the US and China in pursuing a constructive and strategically stable relationship between the world's largest economies," McInerney said.
Visa must complete its preparations within one year, after which it can apply to open for business, the PBOC said.
The central bank, together with the nation's top banking regulator, will review the application and, if it approves, issue a bank card clearing business licence.

Visa was hoping to break into the Chinese market, which is dominated by state-controlled China UnionPay, with an unprecedented 100% ownership stake in a future joint venture licence, sources have told Reuters.

"This should be viewed as a goodwill gesture from Beijing towards Washington ahead of the next meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump," said George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group. The two are expected to meet again on the sidelines of the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in November.

Greater market access in financial services has long been a priority for Washington, which has consistently urged Beijing to provide a more open and level playing field for foreign firms operating in China's financial sector, said Chen.
Mastercard, partnering with local clearinghouse NetsUnion Clearing Corp, won approval to prepare to set up its bank card clearing business in China in 2020.
American Express' joint venture in the country was cleared to start bank card clearing services later that year.

In China, bank cards processed 4.6 trillion transactions worth 963.60 trillion yuan (US$143.92 trillion) in 2025, according to data from the central bank, highlighting the market's enormous potential.
b218b9d97e9d0ab2: SINGAPORE, Oct 13 — Moving to Johor Bahru may seem like a way to escape Singapore’s high cost of living, but one family has found themselves spending even more after relocating across the border.
For Noor Sobri Mohamed Noor, 37, his family’s monthly expenses have risen by about 10 to 20 per cent since they moved to Johor in 2022.
Yet he has no regrets.

According to Berita Minggu, Sobri, who lives in Iskandar Puteri with his wife and five children, said the higher costs largely come from international school fees, which can reach RM3,000 (S$940) per child.
“Financially, our expenses are a little high because of international school fees.
“But in terms of the value of life, we can live in a big house in a gated and guarded estate, which is a big difference compared to in Singapore,” he said.
From dreading life in JB to moving his own family there
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Vehicles (left) travel across the Causeway that connects Malaysia’s southern peninsular state of Johor to the Woodlands immigration checkpoint in Singapore. — AFP pic
Sobri did not always enjoy living in Johor.
Growing up, his parents had chosen to settle in Johor Bahru, even though the family were Singaporeans.
He recalled having to wake up as early as 5am every day to travel from home to his school in Singapore.
When he turned 18 and became eligible for National Service (NS), he “returned” to Singapore.
But almost two decades later, Sobri found himself moving back to the very place he once disliked, and raising a family there.
“As I grew up, I started to see Johor through a different lens,” said the founder of Lufts Barber.
He wanted his five children, aged five to 13, to enjoy a more relaxed and well-rounded education, along with a larger living space.
All five now attend an international school in Tebrau.
Sobri said his children previously struggled with the pace of Singapore’s curriculum, with his eldest son’s mathematics grades declining.
After transferring to the international school, however, his son began enjoying his lessons more and achieved excellent results without needing regular tuition.
Parents seek more holistic education for children
Nur Syafiqah Abdul Rahman, a PropNex real estate agent who moved to Johor in 2023, shared a similar experience.
Her eight-year-old daughter attends Marlborough College Malaysia, where Syafiqah has seen improvements in her studies.
“There are parents who choose international schools in Johor because they want their children to develop holistically through educational activities.

“They get to visit natural spaces, practise drama, public speaking and sports that are integrated directly into school hours, without the pressure of the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE),” she explained.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link, scheduled to start running from February 2027, is expected to make cross-border travel more convenient. — Xinhua pic via AFP
National University of Singapore economist Dr Timothy Wong said education remains a key consideration for Singaporean families thinking about relocating to Johor.

“Education remains a priority for Singaporean families. Despite having to face the hassle of travelling back and forth across borders, they will not compromise on the quality of their children’s education,” he said.
More Singaporeans open to moving
As co-founder of relocation consultancy MoveToMalaysia, Syafiqah has seen an uptick in enquiries from Singaporeans considering life across the Causeway.
She now receives up to 10 enquiries a month, compared with just two to three two years ago.

A free webinar session organised by her team also attracted more than 100 participants, while an in-person event scheduled for Oct 31 has received over 300 initial registrations, with an expected turnout of up to 700 visitors.
However, Syafiqah cautioned that more enquiries do not necessarily translate into immediate relocations.
So far, she has helped about five families move to Johor, with the shortest process taking six months.
The process involves extensive financial planning, registering for schools, as well as having the proper documentation when handling immigration matters.

She advised Singaporean families to rent a home first to assess the suitability of living in Johor – including the challenges of commuting across the border – before making a commitment to purchase property there.
The Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link, scheduled to begin operations in February 2027, is expected to make cross-border travel more convenient.
Higher property demand and better business prospects
Although Johor offers larger homes at comparatively lower prices, demand is also driving up rents in areas popular with Singaporeans.
Syafiqah cited East Ledang and Eco Botanic as examples.
“When I first started renting a semi-detached house here, the price was around RM5,800.
“Now the same unit can reach RM9,000 per month. In terms of the rental market alone, we have seen how high the demand is,” she said.
More business opportunities across the Causeway
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Roslee Tay (right) founded the Football Code Academy in Iskandar Puteri, Johor in January 2026, saw growing demand for structured football training for children. — Picture by Roslee Tay via AsiaOne
Beyond housing and education, Johor is also attracting Singaporean businesses looking to expand.

Commercial property agent and MoveToMalaysia co-founder Shamir Wahid said major corporate investments could create opportunities for smaller businesses, as new companies bring in workers, suppliers and their families.
These opportunities include tuition centres, enrichment programmes, restaurants, fitness centres and professional services.
“In my opinion, one of the biggest opportunities is the ecosystem that is forming. When a large company establishes a foothold in an area, other businesses tend to spring up around it,” he explained.
For Studio Five Group chief executive officer (CEO) Rayden Yuzz, 40, expanding into Johor has been part of his company’s strategy for a decade.
The creative media company opened its first office in Johor Bahru in 2016 to tap Malaysia’s creative talent pool while benefiting from its proximity to Singapore and lower labour costs.
“For us, operating in Singapore and Johor is not just about managing costs, but leveraging the best of both cities.

“The combination of Singapore’s strategic business environment with Malaysia’s diverse creative talent gives us a unique competitive advantage, thus enabling us to offer better services to customers,” he said.
Meanwhile, 34-year-old Roslee Tay founded the Football Code Academy (FCA) in Iskandar Puteri in January 2026 after identifying demand for structured football training for children.
The academy has since served more than 90 families, with players representing over 14 nationalities, including Singapore.
Roslee said Johor’s proximity to Singapore allowed the academy to attract families from both countries while taking advantage of training facilities and more flexible schedules.
“For us, Johor is not just a cheaper alternative to Singapore. We see it as a market with its own potential and identity, where we can build FCA for the long term,” he said.
Shamir believes the two cities can complement each other rather than compete.
Singapore, he said, remains attractive for headquarters, finance and other high-value business functions, while Johor offers more space, a different cost structure and access to Malaysia’s workforce.
Shamir feels that with more large investments entering Johor, opportunities for SMEs in both cities will become increasingly attractive.
“Big companies may make up the first wave,” he said.
“Businesses that provide services to their employees, families, suppliers and communities may be next.” — AsiaOne
1e45fc049b3904df: CUPERTINO: Meta Platforms Inc. released a long-awaited artificial intelligence model on Monday, a milestone that will test whether its multibillion-dollar push to rebuild its AI organization has improved its technology enough to compete among leaders.

Known as Muse Wonder, the new model is the company’s most capable since Meta Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg overhauled his AI operation through an aggressive hiring push that put new talent at the helm.

The company claims the model, dubbed “Watermelon” internally, is a big leap over its own predecessors, with “frontier capabilities” that its leadership say put it on par with OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic PBC’s Claude when it comes to coding, or working through financial or legal questions.

It can be difficult to compare AI models, as some are better at some tasks and worse at others, and benchmarking parameters can be gamed and aren’t necessarily reflective of how the technology performs in the real world. But, if Meta’s claims hold up to outside testing, and Muse Wonder gains traction with researchers and developers, it would mark a significant turnaround for the company, whose models last year fell flat in Silicon Valley.

“These are true frontier models,” said Meta AI Chief Alexandr Wang in an interview on Monday. “We really think they are competitive with the best models out there, and particularly state of the art on personal and professional agentic work.”
Meta’s shares rose as high as 4.7% on the announcement. The stock has gained nearly 9% so far this year through Friday’s close.

Over the last year and a half, Zuckerberg refocused the company’s efforts on advancing in the AI race, including by committing hundreds of billions of dollars to build out the infrastructure needed to support the models, and recruiting Wang to lead the new AI unit as part of a US$14 billion investment into Scale AI .

For Wang, Muse Wonder’s release represents the culmination of that effort. “This is the big moment,” he said. Wang added that Meta has tried to differentiate itself from competitors by focusing on big models for broad, consumer uses. Last month, the company unveiled a personal AI agent known as Muse, which is designed to help with everyday tasks and errands. The new model will soon power the subscription version of that app.

“I think the rest of the ecosystem has been really focused on coding agents,” Wang said. “We do genuinely think that we’ve taken a differentiated focus to make the personal-agent use case really sing.”

Part of that effort has been to create so-called active memory and active focus capabilities that allow an AI agent to remember relevant information about a user over time and keep working when tasks become increasingly difficult. Wang said Muse Wonder can carry information across “days, weeks, months” so users don’t have to re-explain themselves. Its agent also will be able to try new tactics when it runs into problems or dead ends. The result, Wang said, is that Meta’s consumer AI agent will be able to handle more complex, even “ambiguous” tasks in addition to simple requests.

Wang and his Meta Superintelligence Labs team are already looking beyond Muse Wonder. He said MSL has begun work on “larger and more scaled models.” At the same time, the team is trying to shrink the cost of serving that technology to billions of people. Muse Wonder is larger and more expensive to operate than Meta’s smaller Muse Spark models, Wang said, so the company is already developing specialized versions that it hopes will retain much of Wonder’s capabilities while being efficient enough to deploy at massive scale.
For now, Muse Wonder is available to developers through the Meta Model API and Muse Code.
Asked how he would convince skeptics who still doubt Meta has reached the AI frontier, Wang said they should try the model and judge for themselves.
He said he’s not worried about the “haters,” which he regarded with an expletive.
139940583e84c98a: KUALA LUMPUR: Four friends were charged today at the Bandar Baru Bangi magistrates’ court with murder and abetting the murder of a durian seller whose body was found buried in Semenyih last month.
Asrul Siwi, 32; Amirul Maamur Rosli, 27; Amri Rizani Darus, 36; and Indonesian national Rijal Haryono, 47, nodded after the charges were read out to them before magistrate Saira Banu Ashrof Raja.

bf10563d055337c5: The Home Office's latest attempt to speed up asylum decisions with AI has hit an awkward snag: a new report says more than one in five interview summaries checked by experts failed accuracy tests. A 20-page investigation by the Open Rights Group (ORG) claims the department is pressing ahead with AI tools despite concerns about their accuracy, oversight, and promised efficiency gains. The findings, based on Freedom of Information requests and correspondence with ministers, concern two systems used by Home Office caseworkers: Asylum Case Summarisation (ACS), which summarizes asylum interviews, and Asylum Policy Search (APS), a chat-style tool helping officials search country policy information. Both use OpenAI's GPT-4o model through Microsoft's Azure AI Foundry. The government insists humans remain responsible for asylum decisions, but ORG questions how reliably caseworkers can spot mistakes in AI-generated information. Figures obtained by the campaign group show that 45 of 203 AI-generated interview summaries failed initial expert checks after the system was rolled out in April 2026. That's a 22 percent failure rate, compared with the 9 percent rejection rate recorded during the original pilot. Another 19 summaries were flagged for further review. The figures also record 56 second-stage reviews, of which 30 failed to meet the required standard. The errors can include factual inaccuracies and misrepresentations of what asylum seekers said during interviews. ORG also found that summaries could pass the checks even if they omitted important details, as long as the information they did include was accurate. Despite those results, relatively few summaries have been examined. ORG estimates that Home Office experts checked only 0.3 percent between April and July, based on the department's projected monthly caseload of 17,515. ORG also questioned whether the tools were saving much time. It says the average monthly number of initial substantive asylum decisions since April 2026 fell about 42 percent compared with the same period in 2025, while the mean time from interview to decision rose 29 percent. While those figures don't prove that AI caused the slowdown, they offer little evidence of the productivity gains ministers have promised. Oversight of the separate Asylum Policy Search tool also appears lacking. The Home Office confirmed in August that expert testing had stopped, despite previously telling MPs that checks were continuing. ORG says no summary of the testing results was produced. Meanwhile, asylum applicants are not specifically told when AI has been used in their cases and cannot inspect or correct the summaries generated from their interviews. ORG also questions the Home Office's claims of human oversight. The department's own data protection assessment says ACS automates work previously done by technical specialists, who reviewed and summarized asylum cases before passing them to decision-makers. ORG warns the tool could remove an experienced layer of scrutiny, rather than simply save staff time. The group is calling for both tools to be suspended and independently audited, arguing that the current safeguards are inadequate for decisions that determine whether someone can remain in the UK. It's not the first time the Home Office's technology plans have come under fire. In June, more than 60 rights groups urged ministers to abandon plans for AI-powered age estimation of asylum-seeking children, warning that the technology was unreliable around the crucial 16-to-18-year-old age range. Later that month, an inspection found that the department's long-delayed Atlas immigration system was failing to provide caseworkers with feedback from asylum appeals, forcing staff to rely on workarounds. The Home Office did not respond to The Register's questions. ®
99b038d06ce71815: PETALING JAYA: Police have launched an investigation after several houses inhabited by the Rohingya community in Kulai, Johor, were torched with Molotov cocktails past midnight today.
Johor police chief Ab Rahaman Arsad said a report was lodged at around 1.30am today after the firebombing occurred, causing minor fires at the gates of the houses.
He said the fires were put out swiftly and no injuries or property damage were reported.
Rahaman said investigations showed the incident might have been in response to two viral videos purportedly showing a group of Rohingya men daring people to a fight in Kulai.
"A Rohingya man in his 30s has lodged a police report denying involvement in the videos. He claimed that his picture was misused by others to produce the video," he said in a statement.

Rahaman said police were investigating the firebombing for mischief by fire as well as the spread of the viral videos for improper use of network facilities and statements conducing to public mischief.
a5dc563fdbb629c2: NEW YORK, Oct 13 — US actress Selma Blair was arrested after an alleged altercation on a flight from Los Angeles to New York City that injured at least two cabin crew members, authorities said Monday.
The Legally Blonde and Cruel Intentions star was detained at John F Kennedy Airport after her Delta Air Lines flight landed late Sunday following reports of a physically abusive passenger.
US media said that Blair punched one flight attendant and bit another. The 54-year-old then reportedly assaulted a police officer and nurse as she was transported to hospital.
“Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct,” a representative for Blair said.
“Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition.”
The FBI issued a summons accusing Blair of assaults on the plane, according to a federal judicial source.
Blair was arraigned on two counts of second-degree assault Monday night and was released on bail. A new hearing in the case is scheduled for January 19, 2027.
A spokesperson for Delta said the airline “has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behaviour, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first.”
In 2016, Blair was removed from a plane on a stretcher after another outburst on a flight.
“I mixed alcohol with medication, and that caused me to black out and led me to say and do things that I deeply regret,” she told Vanity Fair after that incident.
She also described in her 2022 memoir having bitten several celebrities, including Kate Moss, often in situations where she had been drinking alcohol. — AFP
d51f5bf94d754bd3: KUALA LUMPUR: Empat rakan didakwa di Mahkamah Majistret Bandar Baru Bangi hari ini atas pertuduhan membunuh dan bersubahat dalam pembunuhan seorang penjual durian yang mayatnya ditemukan ditanam di Semenyih, Selangor, bulan lepas.

Asrul Siwi, 32, Amirul Maamur Rosli, 27, Amri Rizani Darus, 36, dan warga Indonesia Rijal Haryono, 47, mengangguk faham selepas pertuduhan ke atas mereka dibacakan di hadapan Majistret Saira Banu Mohamed Ashrof Raja.
Tiada pengakuan direkodkan kerana kesalahan bunuh berada di bawah bidang kuasa Mahkamah Tinggi.

Mengikut pertuduhan, Asrul dan Amirul Maamur bersama tiga lagi individu yang masih bebas didakwa membunuh Mulialisman Nordi, 34, di Batu 28, Sungai Lalang, Mukim Ulu Semenyih di Hulu Langat, antara 24 dan 25 Sept lepas.
Pertuduhan dikemukakan mengikut Seksyen 302 Kanun Keseksaan dibaca bersama Seksyen 34 akta sama yang memperuntukkan hukuman mati atau penjara antara 30 hingga 40 tahun dan minimum 12 sebatan.

Dua lagi tertuduh, Amri Rizani dan Rijal pula didakwa bersubahat membantu Asrul dan Amirul Maamur membunuh mangsa dengan cara melarikan si mati serta membantu mengasah cangkul di tempat dan masa yang sama.
Mereka didakwa mengikut Seksyen 109 Kanun Keseksaan dibaca bersama Seksyen 302 akta sama yang membawa hukuman serupa, jika sabit kesalahan.
Pendakwaan dikendalikan oleh Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Nurul Atiqah Mohamad Alias manakala kesemua tertuduh tidak diwakili peguam.
Mahkamah tidak membenarkan sebarang jaminan ditawarkan kepada tertuduh dan menetapkan 1 Dis depan sebagai tarikh sebutan semula kes.

8a5b22033364fd65: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Schools in Johor, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan will stay closed tomorrow, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek announced today, as haze continues to affect parts of the country.

Schools under nine district education offices (PPD) in Selangor, Pahang, Sabah and Sarawak will also be shut. They are Hulu Langat and Sepang in Selangor; Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin in Pahang; Tawau in Sabah; and Serian, Sri Aman and Lubok Antu in Sarawak.

Today’s closures covered Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan and Putrajaya, along with the Hulu Langat, Petaling Perdana, Kuala Langat and Sepang PPDs in Selangor and the Kuantan and Rompin PPDs in Pahang. Pekan and the Sabah and Sarawak districts were not on that list.
During the closure, all pupils, including those in hostels, will follow Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) so that learning continues, in line with the ministry’s directive.
Parents and guardians were urged to make sure their children take part in PdPR.
The extension comes even though air quality in the state has eased.

According to Department of Environment (DOE) data as of 10.40am today, Seremban's API fell from 167 yesterday afternoon to 154, while Nilai dropped from 164 to 151. Port Dickson, which logged 154 yesterday, was no longer in the unhealthy range. An API reading of 101 to 200 is classed as unhealthy.
Nationwide, 20 of the 68 monitoring stations recorded unhealthy readings this morning, down from 23 yesterday.

Johor remained the worst affected, with eight unhealthy stations. Pasir Gudang recorded the highest reading in the country at 181, up from 174, followed by Larkin at 176 and Sri Aman in Sarawak at 170. No station recorded very unhealthy or hazardous levels.
Health and education authorities have advised parents, high-risk groups and students with respiratory ailments to wear face masks outdoors and to follow API updates through official channels.

c82e6ff351d5cfbf: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 13 — Malaysia needs to brace itself for the Super El Niño phenomenon, which is expected to bring scorching weather between March and May next year, potentially breaking the country’s record high temperature of 40.1 degrees Celsius.

Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the country’s maximum temperature could exceed 41 degrees Celsius, based on analysis of the current intense El Niño phenomenon, alongside the impacts of climate change and global warming.
“If we look at current climate change trends, the rate of temperature increase in the country is approximately 0.13 degrees Celsius per decade.

“It has been nearly 30 years since 1998, when combined with the temperature spikes associated with El Niño, the increase could exceed one degree Celsius above the 40.1-degree record set back then. We anticipate that temperatures reaching 41 degrees Celsius or higher are likely to occur. That is our projection,” he said.

He made these remarks at a press conference following the National Climate Forum 2026 at Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) here today. The forum, themed “Preparedness Today, Resilience Tomorrow,” was attended by over 500 participants from various government departments and ministries.

Malaysia previously recorded its highest-ever temperature of 40.1 degrees Celsius in Chuping, Perlis, on April 9, 1998, during the 1997/1998 El Niño episode, while the peak temperature during the 2015/2016 episode was 39.3 degrees Celsius, recorded in Batu Embun, Pahang, on April 10, 2016.
Mohd Hisham said the current El Niño is projected to record an index exceeding 2.5, surpassing the peak level of 2.3 recorded during the 1997/1998 and 2015/2016 episodes.

He noted that during strong El Niño events, daily maximum temperatures can rise by up to 0.7 degrees Celsius above normal, while temperatures exceeding 35 degrees Celsius are expected to occur more widely and for longer periods.
Mohd Hisham added that the previously recorded scenario of up to 77 consecutive days without rain could recur particularly in the northern states of the Peninsula due to this El Niño phenomenon.

“Previous records show that this condition can begin at the end of the year, with a lack of rainfall starting in December and continuing through January and February, before rain returns around March,” he said.

In this regard, he emphasised that the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon currently forecast to begin in late October is crucial for ensuring dams receive sufficient rainfall and water storage levels are boosted before the country faces drier weather next year.
“We must ensure all our dams are full before next year begins. In terms of water sources, the Northeast Monsoon brings significant rainfall, and we hope this rain will fill all the dams,” he said.

He said this measure aligns with the directive from Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr. Ahmad Zahid Hamidi to make early preparations regarding water supply and storage in anticipation of the hot and dry spell next year.
Mohd Hisham also expressed concern regarding the anticipated rise in electricity consumption during next year’s hot weather, particularly due to the expected increase in air conditioner usage.

“Energy consumption will be high during the hot months next year. Therefore, regarding the energy grid, we must ensure there is sufficient capacity. A lack of preparedness could lead to disruptions and compromise the grid,” he said.

He said MetMalaysia has informed relevant agencies of this forecast, and the matter will be raised at the Disaster Management Council meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim next week.

At the same time, he noted that MetMalaysia is collaborating with the Ministry of Health (MOH) to develop a Heat Index. This will establish threshold values used to warn the public about health risks associated with hot weather.

He explained that the current hot weather monitoring system classifies temperatures of 35 degrees Celsius and above as Level 1, 37 degrees Celsius and above as Level 2, and 40 degrees Celsius and above as Level 3. — Bernama

a37c1648fc8eb00d: VMware has discovered so many flaws in its products using AI that it felt the need to create a new product to help users manage them. Prashanth Shenoy, vice president of product marketing in the VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) division of Broadcom, told The Register that VMware recently moved to deliver monthly software updates, in part to address bugs found by AI. He admitted, however, that users struggled to keep up with the pace of change before the move to monthly releases because it takes time to test the impact of patches – even though VCF allows non-disruptive live patching. Shenoy said customers therefore need "room to breathe." Enter a new tool called HyperArmor, which does three things. One is "virtual patching" – blocking attempts to exploit a vulnerability without changing the vulnerable software itself. VMware already offers virtual patching in its vDefend network security product and explains how it works by referring to CVE-2024-5806, the bug in file transfer tool MOVEIt that made waves in 2024. VMware says vDefend can detect patterns associated with attempts to exploit the authentication bypass flaw and block the traffic. HyperArmor will do similar things to block malicious traffic heading toward VCF implementations. Another job HyperArmor takes on is rejecting any actions that alter known good states in VCF. If a human approves a change, the tool will update policies to allow the altered state. The third job is multi-factor authentication (MFA). The Register put it to Shenoy that MFA is now table stakes for security. He agreed but explained that VMware designed HyperArmor to protect against attackers using stolen privileged credentials to access VMware's ESX hypervisor. To (hopefully) stop attackers using those creds to take over a host, HyperArmor requires users to input SSH credentials and a secondary time-based one-time password sent to a user with a verified identity. HyperArmor is a discrete product that VMware will sell as an add-on to VCF. That means VMware thinks its customers are going to be OK paying extra for MFA. While VMware will sell HyperArmor, it didn't create the product. Broadcom's security businesses Symantec and Carbon Black cooked it up. Broadcom's CA business (formerly Computer Associates) has done similar things. At VMware Explore on August 31, Broadcom launched AgentMinder, which aims to stop AI running inside VCF going rogue. AgentMinder came from CA but was launched as a tool for VCF (and third-party Kubernetes stacks). At VMware Explore, The Register met Ram Velaga, president of Broadcom's Infrastructure Software Group, and asked him if the group has a single strategy, or if its divisions each do their own thing. Velaga said Broadcom uses a combination of both approaches. "There's a level of focus with individual teams that you don't have if you have one very large central team," he said. "You get the speed at which you have to innovate with individual teams." Broadcom's Infrastructure Software Group therefore operates with at least six teams, and when one of those teams wants to add functions it will look for existing assets developed by another internal team rather than trying to write its own code. For broad products like VCF, the work of several Broadcom teams could therefore be relevant. The Register has no idea which team created the name HyperArmor, a question we pose as Cisco already offers a "Hypershield." Maybe this sort of name is what's needed to stop a HyperHoodie? ®

bbe9efcd05754558: When government officials craft policies, there is often a comment period for public feedback. Lawmakers have long had to sort through fake feedback that is mass-produced in an effort to sway policy, but they’ve generally gotten used to detecting it. With, artificial intelligence, however, people can submit realistic-seeming comments, which are harder to dismiss as being fabrications with no person behind them. That’s just one way AI can be used to generate text and statements, in civic conversations, for which no one can be found to be answerable. This issue, among others, has caught the attention of Deb Roy, professor of media arts and sciences at MIT and director of the MIT Center for Constructive Communication (CCC). In a new essay published in the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, titled, “Who stands behind the words?,” Roy calls for a renewed emphasis on responsibility in communication, asserting that even when AI is used to craft text, there needs to be accountability and “answerability.” Building better group dialogues to produce more public trust is a core part of the work of CCC. The group, along with Cortico, the closely affiliated nonprofit Roy co-founded, has helped facilitate group discussions on important issues in many situations — including civic meetings, schools, deliberative assemblies, and private organizations — and used tech tools, including AI, to help find themes among comments, and more. But the center also designs this process so that participants can check and override the tech-based output at each key step. Ultimately, a person is responsible for every public comment. MIT News spoke to Roy about the essay and the work of the center.  Q: You’ve identified this problem about the lack of accountability behind words that are generated by AI. When did you really first notice this? A: It came into focus when Chat-GPT [which is powered by a large language model, or LLM] launched. As for my own history with language models, my PhD work explored what we might now call PLMs — Puny Language Models — so I’m quite familiar with language models and have tracked the field’s rapid evolution. But Chat-GPT turned a corner. Two things changed at the same time: the depth of the model and its knowledge, and the way you could interact with it.  I became obsessed with trying to find the limits of what it could do. And I felt that no matter how hard I tried to stretch my arms around it, I couldn’t. I built my tenure case at MIT on language grounding — the idea that it’s not enough for an AI system to just process lots of words and other symbols. I believed that to understand what words mean, you actually need a physical body and life experiences as part of the process. So I revisited the philosophy-of-AI literature I had once been steeped in, which asks what fundamentally distinguishes the kind of system that large language models exemplify, in extraordinarily advanced form, from the kind of processing we humans engage in. I gave several presentations to my own graduate students trying to make the case that, even though AI seems so intelligent, it’s actually different in kind — and I could not convince them.  And I thought, I know the difference, but I’m having trouble convincing even myself of what it is. And that led me to ask, “Wait a minute: Is there someone or something that stands behind the words, a human responsible for what is being said?” That’s the thing this extraordinary new language machine doesn’t have.  Whether these systems genuinely understand language is actively debated. But even if you grant them all the comprehension you like, they still lack standing. The buck can’t stop at a thing, a software system, with nothing to lose. Q: The Bulletin piece has these interesting examples of civic feedback forums where it looks like there are real people saying things, and instead you have a barrage of comments from AI. How did you find some of these other examples in society where things go off the rails in this way?  A: After the release of ChatGPT, I started hearing a concern from people inside government who review public comments on proposed rules: a suspicion that not all of the comments were written by humans. My reaction was: That’s going to delegitimize this channel for public feedback. That was several years ago, but everyone now knows this is happening. Public comment is a pillar of democracy. You don’t just put a new rule in place. People need to have a voice and feel like they’ve been heard before a rule is imposed on them. If you skip that step, people don’t accept rules as legitimate. That’s why that process is baked into how America works. And that pillar just cracked, and by now, in my mind, it’s fallen over. Has anyone noticed? My sense is the people on the receiving end of these comments have quietly adjusted the weight they give to public comments. It was never perfect, but boy, now much of its value is being swept away.  I open my essay with this example: In 2017, the Federal Communications Commission received more than 22 million public comments on its proposal to repeal net neutrality rules, and the New York attorney general later found that nearly 18 million of them were fake. As I write in the essay, “That fraud was caught because it left fingerprints: templated text, duplicated phrasing.” But large language models erase the fingerprints. Now every comment can be fluent and different, and reviewers can no longer tell which ones express views that real people formed and stand behind. If you have enough of the stuff that’s fake — words that no one with a stake actually stands behind — it desensitizes you to what’s real. That filters back to the public, and people realize: If I take the time to express myself, they’re not even listening any more. Q: Could you say a little bit more about your point that we need people with “standing,” who will take “accountability” for all pieces of text, even when those bits of text are generated by AI?  A: In the legal system, standing is a formal idea: sometimes a case isn’t heard because the people bringing it don’t have standing. But informally we use that term all the time. I’m not trying to formalize standing in everyday life. Instead I’m asking:  What is the informal sense of the term, borrowed from the legal one, that we need to pay more attention to now? Here in New England, consider the open town meeting: The person who stands up to speak is generally expected to have standing, as someone from that town with a stake in what gets decided. And if it’s a stranger who drove from across the state, or from out of state, everyone’s like: Wait a minute, who is that? They’re not from around here. In general, there’s just enough friction and it’s costly enough to show up somewhere you don’t actually have standing, that it doesn’t happen much. Now LLMs and the current digital networked environment collapse those boundaries. We always took for granted that if someone has a voice, it’s because they have standing. They have some basis to be heard. We need to pay attention to this, and really consider how to design systems so that the people with standing are the ones who get heard.  The other idea I tried to develop is “answerability.” It isn’t formalized in law, but it’s baked into the legal process. If you have standing to give testimony, there you are, ready for cross-examination. You have to be able to answer for what you’re saying. And if you’re making a specific accusation about someone, you have to be willing to back it with facts. Standing and answerability have to travel together: The right to be heard comes with the obligation to answer for what you say. That doesn’t mean everyone has to attach their name to everything. I write in the Bulletin essay, “Privacy and answerability aren’t opposites. … An institution can verify a person and stand behind their words without exposing them.” To voice a view, you only need to show that a distinct, eligible person is speaking. An accusation asks more: Someone trusted, like a reporter, has to be able to know who is speaking. As I say: “Disclosure obligations should scale with power, and identity protections with vulnerability.” None of this means AI can’t help. AI can do a lot of the work inside the chain of accountability — drafting, summarizing, finding patterns. If someone with a stake in a rule uses AI to draft a comment, adopts it as their own, and is ready to answer for it, that’s legitimate, in this context. What AI can’t do is anchor the chain. There has to be a person at the end who stands behind the words. In the essay I lay out four design principles for building that in: “attributable authorship,” a “decomposed and inspectable process,” the use of “provenance as infrastructure,” and the need to “widen standing rather than concentrating it.” As I write, the “animating rule is that autonomy is permitted while unaccountability is not.” And the metric that matters most isn’t the efficiency gained by removing humans, but the number of people AI places into roles where they can answer for what they do. Q: There is a phrase in the documents of the Center for Constructive Communication, that we need things to move “at the speed of trust,” not at the “speed of tech.” And that implies really thinking about building up these systems. Could you just say a little more about what that phrase means to you? A: I learned that phrase when I was in Appleton, Wisconsin, with Katherine Cramer [of the University of Wisconsin], a longtime collaborator, talking with community organizers who were running “Dialogue across Divides” conversations there. They had hundreds of people involved. I thought I was developing technology tools with exactly that same purpose, and was so excited to see it. And I asked one of the people who ran that organization, “How fast did you scale this?” And he paused, and then he said, “At the speed of trust.”  And I took that to mean “slow.” Then I realized he was saying: For you, slow, because you haven’t yet earned our trust. And I’ve since learned that when you do have trust, things can move fast. So bringing in technology is really a process of engagement. It doesn’t work to say, “Trust us, we’re doing this because we think it’s for your own good.” People will turn to someone they already trust and ask, “Is this good for us?” And if that person says “Yes,” things can move fast. Look at what’s happening at the intersection of AI and society: The speed of AI and the speed of democracy are running on different clocks. Talk to people who work in democratic practice and they say, “AI must slow down, because democracy can’t move that fast.” Talk to people in AI and they say, “AI cannot slow down, democracy needs to speed up.” If we can’t get these two time scales in sync, we’re headed for a breakway situation, where AI gets deployed faster than democratic processes can respond, and decisions get made without the public. That’s starting to happen right now.  Q: We need people actively doing things to build dialogue and figure out how tech tools can interact with that. At the Center for Constructive Communication, you’ve done a few iterations of the center’s Real Talk initiatives to build civic dialogues, as well as the Youth Voices Initiative in school settings, and currently you’re working on the New Social Forms project. Could you say a few words about them?  A: The Real Talk effort represents the longest-standing thread in this work. A huge emphasis of our work has been developing better ways to listen to one another. We create a context that is always small — small is beautiful here — where people are willing to share authentically. And we have the consent architecture and the technology to reveal the larger patterns, and then share them. We’ve done this with hundreds of communities around the country. And closer to home, we’ve brought the same approach to our campus here at MIT through the realtalk@MIT program, with support from the Office of the President and the Office of the Provost, to help our community build a culture around dialogue and listening.  The second thing I’d emphasize is that we’ve been doing more and more work on deliberative processes and citizen assemblies, and on how to make them more accessible. What if a group of high schoolers says, “We have a real problem with our cellphone policy?” Suppose you want to have an assembly that brings students, teachers, and administrators together, not just to listen to people’s concerns but to make policy recommendations. So we did that. The center worked with a high school in New York City, where technology helped people reveal their preferences and differences and listen to each other. We’re also building answerability into the technology. A prototype called VoiceTrace, developed by PhD student Cassandra Overney in our group, links every output statement — a summary of what was heard in a listening process, or a recommendation coming out of a deliberation — to the specific voices behind it, so any claim can be traced back to the conversations it came from. The New Social Forms project pertains to a very interesting pattern emerging in workplaces around the world, certainly the ones we’re connected to. AI is an extraordinary tool for individual empowerment, but in the words of one of our collaborators at the Google Experience Institute, people are tunneling. They go deep, using AI to develop refined ideas, but when they surface, their ideas have diverged from their teammates’. So groups and teams trying to work together with AI, there’s a human coordination problem. We’re going to expand the initial work we’ve started with Google because there’s a lot of interest in collective communication, trust, and interaction among people trying to work together.  So is that a civic context? It’s a workplace, but workplaces are civic spaces, too. They govern people’s daily lives, they’re where many of us build civic skills and learn to cooperate across difference, and there’s a long tradition of civic life rooted in shared work. We’re all humans trying to interact with each other. These are the same issues. Justice Louis Brandeis once used the phrase “industrial democracy” to capture this. When workplaces lacked certain kinds of civic processes and civility — two interestingly related terms — labor disputes used to turn violent. Procedural justice, mediators, and people hearing one another are just as necessary in the workplace. In the end, it’s all about human beings. Hearing the humanity in one another is what democracy depends on, and it’s just as necessary for communities and organizations to function.
